http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 | page= | quote = }} |- |後身校 | style="background:white;" |[[日本大学]] |} '''日本法律学校'''（にほんほうりつがっこう）は、[[1889年]]（[[明治]]22年）10月に[[東京市]][[麹町区]][[飯田橋|飯田町]]の[[皇典講究所]]内に設立設立認可。された[[私立学校|私立]][[法律学校 (旧制)|法律学校]]。[[大日本帝国憲法]]公布にともない、[[皇典講究所]]所長である[[法務大臣|司法大臣]][[山田顕義]]が、[[日本]]の[[法律]]を研究し国運の増進をはかる目的とする学校の設立をめざし、同じ趣旨で学校設立計画を進める法律学者らを全面的に支援して設立された。この項目では後身である日本大学（[[専門学校令]]準拠）についても扱う。 == 概要 == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|[[皇典講究所]]発祥記念碑]] 現在の'''[[日本大学]]の前身'''である私立法律学校である。現在の日大では本校の設立認可がなされた1889年10月4日を大学創立の日付とし、この日は同大学の「創立記念日」として継承されている 日本法律学校の設立認可からちょうど100年後の[[1989年]]（平成元年）10月4日には、[[上皇明仁|明仁天皇]]および[[上皇后美智子|美智子皇后]]の臨席のもと日本大学の創立百周年記念式典が挙行されている。{{Cite web|和書| author = 天皇・皇后| title = 主な式典におけるおことば（平成元年） | publisher = [[宮内庁]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。日大の学部・学科のうち[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]法律学科および[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|文理学部]]は「日本法律学校」時代に、法学部政治経済学科・[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]は[[専門学校令]]準拠時代（[[旧制専門学校]]としての日本大学時代）にまでその起源を遡ることができる。 [[1889年]]（明治22年）[[4月3日]]の「日本法律学校設立趣意書」の趣意では、「外来の先進ヨーロッパ諸国の法学思想とわが国固有の思想との融合調和を目指し、日本独自の法律文化を確立するため、法学教育の機関を創設すべき必要がある」とし、主意書に記されている創立目的を要約すると、「日本の法律は新旧を問わず学ぶ、海外の法律を参考として長所を取り入れる、日本法学という学問を提唱する」とした。[[近代国家]]の成立期、従来のように欧米法教育が主流の時代において、日本法律を教育する学校として誕生した本校は独自性を発揮することとなった。 開校当初は、[[皇典講究所]]の校舎を借り受けて授業を行うなど、同所および同所内に設立された[[國學院]]と深い関係を有していた。また設立当初行っていた夜間授業は最初に認可されたものである。 == 沿革 == === 設立時の経緯 === [[ファイル:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|学祖・[[山田顕義]]]] [[ファイル:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|創立者総代・[[宮崎道三郎]]]] [[ファイル:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|初代校長・[[金子堅太郎]]]] [[ファイル:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|第2代校長、初代総長・[[松岡康毅]]]] [[1889年]]（明治22年2月11日に[[大日本帝国憲法]]が発布されると、[[法学|法学界]]の中から'''外国の法理論は参考とし、日本の法律を中心に研究することを趣旨とする学校の設立'''を求める声が起こった。当時、初代[[法務大臣|司法大臣]]の任にあった[[山田顕義]]は、日本最初となるこの憲法の施行に向け日本独自の[[法典]]研究と教育が急務であると考え、自らが所長を兼ねていた[[皇典講究所]]内に「[[国法]]科」を新設することを構想した。また同時期、山田とは別に[[東京大学|東京帝国大学]]教授・[[宮崎道三郎]]を中心とする若手の法律学者らによって日本法律を教授する学校の設立の計画が進められていた。これらを契機として、山田は宮崎や憲法起草者である[[金子堅太郎]]ら法学者11名と協議し、新たな理念と思想を持つ法律学校設立のための設立要旨を次のように取りまとめた。 「一、国法は日本固有の国体・民情・慣習・ 文化を根底として作らるべきであり，この際日本古来の慣習制度をみ直す　二、憲法はじめ法律が多数制定されつつある現在，これを国民に熟知徹底させるために日本法律を講義する　三、日本法律として成立した法律を検討し，古来の精神・慣習・制度の面から必要な改正の議をたてる　四、同時に海外の法理もまた大いに研究し，わが国法学に資し，もって日本法学を振起して国運の増進をはかる」。 上記の設立要旨をもって1889年9月、[[東京府]]に設立許可が申請され、同年10月4日に設立が認可された日本法律学校は、翌年の[[1890年]]9月、設立者の一人である金子堅太郎を初代校長に迎えて開校した。開校当初、本校は皇典講究所の校舎内に設置され、同所の校舎（教室）を夜間借り受けて講義を行なう形式をとっていたが、これは同じ年の1890年、皇典講究所内に国史・国文・国法を教授する[[國學院]]が開校したことにともない、当初の山田の構想に沿って同校において国法を専修し法典研究にあたる部局として位置づけられていたためである{{Cite web|和書| author = | title = 学部・学科等の理念・目的 - 國學院大學 | publisher = | date = | url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf | accessdate = 2016-02-23 | page= 6 | quote =}}。 一方、設立評議員となった山田顕義は、設立時に示した開学理念による思想的影響に止まらず、運営財政面を中心にさまざまな形で本校の設立事業とその後の学校の発展に大きく貢献した。彼の支援によって設立時には[[司法省 (日本)|司法省]]から「法律取調事業嘱託費」の名目で50,000円の下付がなされただけでなく、設立後にも彼は[[文部省]]に対して「特別認可学校」とするよう要請を行った。さらに彼はさまざまな近代法典編纂に関わり日本における「近代法の祖」と称されていることから、本校の後身機関である日本大学は彼に「'''学祖'''」の称号を与え、大学の歴史上特別な位置づけとしている。 === 皇典講究所からの独立 === [[1892年]]11月11日、庇護者である山田が死去すると資金難が予想されたため本学は廃校も協議されるようになり、卒業生46名を送り出した[[1893年]]7月の第1回卒業式の直前には金子校長が辞職する事態となった。しかし卒業生の運動もあって本学はこの危機を乗り切り、1893年12月には[[司法省 (日本)#指定学校|司法省指定学校]]とされ[[松岡康毅]]が第2代校長に就任し、学校経営を安定させることに成功した。そして[[1897年]]には学術研究の機関誌として『日本法政新誌』が創刊されるなど、法律学校としての体裁も次第に整備された。これらと並行して[[1895年]]～[[1896年]]の校地移転、および1896年12月の[[財団法人]]改組を通じて皇典講究所からの組織的独立も果たした。 === 「日本大学」と改称 === 当初法律学科現在の[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|日大法学部]]法律学科の前身。のみを設置していた本学は、[[1901年]]10月に[[高等師範学校|高等師範科]]現在の[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|日大文理学部]]の前身。を設置して単なる法律学校に止まらない[[総合大学]]への昇格を目指すようになり、[[1903年]]8月、'''[[日本大学]]と改称'''し、翌[[1904年]]に[[専門学校令]]準拠の高等教育機関となり、併せて大学部に政治科・商科それぞれ現在の法学部政治経済学科、および[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]の前身。を併設した。 なお、校名を日本法律学校から日本大学に改めることに[[文部省]]は難色を示し、理事の[[戸水寛人]]を呼びつけて「日本法律学校なら日本の法律を教える学校なので問題ないが、日本大学だと[[大日本帝国|日本]]を代表する[[旧官立大学|国立大学]]と間違えられる恐れがある」として再考を求めた。しかし戸水は承服せず、「日本大学が駄目なら[[日本学園中学校・高等学校|日本中学]]はどうなるのか」と主張し、ついに日本大学への改称を認めさせたというエピソードが知られている[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ 日本大学への改称に尽力 戸水 寛人｜日本大学の歴史][[河岡潮風]] 『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 東都游学学校評判記]』 [[博文館]]、1909年、143-144頁『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、497-498頁。 === 大学昇格への道 === この時点では制度上[[旧制専門学校]]であった日本大学が[[大学令]]による制度上の大学（[[旧制大学]]）に昇格したのは、[[1920年]]（大正9年）4月16日である。そして、専門学校令準拠の日本大学は在籍者の卒業を待って1922年度いっぱいで廃止された『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、77頁。 == 年表 == [[File:日本法律学校（1896年頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|日本法律学校（1896年頃）]] [[File:1912年（明治45年）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|1912年改築の校舎]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|三崎町校舎（1920年竣工）]] * [[1889年]]（明治22年） ** 9月 - [[東京府]]に日本法律学校の設立許可が申請される。 ** 10月4日 -''' 設立認可'''。 * [[1890年]]（明治23年）9月 - 金子堅太郎を初代校長として開校式挙行。 * [[1893年]]（明治26年） ** 7月16日 - 第1回卒業生46名。 ** 12月 - 司法省指定学校となり判事検事登用試験の受験資格が与えられる。 *[[1895年]]（明治28年）- 校舎を大日本教育会（[[神田区]][[一ツ橋]]通）内に移転。 *[[1897年]]（明治30年）1月 - 学術研究誌『'''日本法政新誌'''』第1号が刊行。 *[[1898年]]（明治31年）12月22日 - [[財団法人]]組織に改組し、皇典講究所から組織的独立当時、[[財団法人]]化にしたのは本校が最初である。。 * [[1901年]]（明治34年）10月 - 高等師範科設置。 * [[1903年]]（明治36年） ** 2月 - 高等予備科・高等法学科を設置。 ** 8月19日 - [[校則]]を改め'''大学組織「日本大学」に改称'''。記念して徽章と制服・制帽を制定。 ** 12月 - 外国語専修部（英語・ドイツ語専修科）を設置。 * [[1904年]]（明治37年） ** 3月 - [[専門学校令]]準拠の[[旧制専門学校]]となり、従前の大学部法律学科と並んで政治科・商科を併設。 ** 10月 - 大学部法律学科・政治科・商科に在籍する学生総数は1,800名、教員総数約80名であった。 * [[1905年]]（明治38年）10月 - 大学部商科の授業開始『日本大学商学部百年史』 69頁。 * [[1911年]]（明治44年）4月 - 大学部・専門部の政治科の授業開始『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、508-510頁。 * [[1917年]]（大正{{0}}6年）4月 - 予科の[[修業年限]]を2年に延長。 * [[1920年]]（大正{{0}}9年）4月16日 - '''[[大学令]]準拠の[[旧制大学|（旧制）大学]]として発足'''。法文学部（法律科・政治科・宗教科・社会科）と商学部（商科）を設置。 * [[1923年]]（大正12年）3月 - 専門学校令準拠の大学部・大学予科を廃止。 == 創立に関わった人物 == 日本大学の「学祖」とされる山田顕義が創立に深く関わっている。 === 設立評議員 === * [[山田顕義]] * [[箕作麟祥]] * [[加藤弘之]] * [[穂積八束]] * [[児島惟謙]] * [[松岡康毅]] * [[清浦奎吾]] * [[中村元嘉]] === 創立者 === * [[宮崎道三郎]]（創立者総代） * [[金子堅太郎]]（初代校長） * [[樋山資之]]（幹事） * [[斯波淳六郎]]（幹事） * [[野田藤吉郎]]（幹事） * [[本多康直]] * [[末岡精一]] * [[添田寿一]] * [[穂積八束]] * [[平島及平]] * [[上條慎蔵]] == 歴代校長・学長・総長 == * 初代：[[金子堅太郎]]（[[1890年]]10月～[[1893年]]7月） * 第2代：[[松岡康毅]]（1893年12月～[[1923年]]9月）[[1903年]]8月に専門学校令準拠の日本大学学長、[[1920年]]4月に大学令準拠の日本大学学長、[[1922年]]3月に総長となった。 == 校地の変遷と継承 == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|日本大学開校の地（[[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）]] 設立時の校地は、先述の通り皇典講究所のあった[[東京市]]'''[[麹町区]]飯田町'''（現在の[[東京都]][[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）に所在し、木造2階建ての校舎を昼は國學院が、夜は日本法律学校が使用していた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、336-337頁。 山田没後の[[1895年]]（明治28年）10月に[[神田区]][[一ツ橋|一ツ橋通町]]（現・[[千代田区]][[一ツ橋]]2丁目）の[[大日本教育会]]内の一室を借りて移転したが、間もなく大日本教育会に合併話が持ち上がり、教室の継続使用ができなくなったため、翌年6月[[神田区]][[神田三崎町|三崎町]]3丁目の練兵場跡地の校舎に移転して皇典講究所から独立した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、401-406頁。当初の敷地は約220坪、建坪は約160坪。3つの教室と講師室、事務室などが設けられていたに過ぎなかったが、明治30年代には増築を重ねて6部屋の教室を擁する2階建て校舎となり『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、409頁、[[1912年]]（明治45年）にも改築の手が加えられた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695頁。 [[1918年]]（大正7年）には創立30周年記念事業の一環として新校舎の建設構想が浮上した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695-702頁。[[大学令]]による認可条件として施設整備は必須だったため、[[1919年]]（大正8年）12月に起工、認可間もない[[1920年]]（大正9年）5月に新校舎落成式、大正8年度卒業式、校友大会を兼ねた昇格祝賀会を行った『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、87-96頁。 三崎町校舎は現在の日本大学神田三崎町キャンパス（[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]および両学部管轄の大学院研究科が所在）に継承されている。旧飯田町校舎の所在地は現在、'''「日本大学開校の地」の碑'''が建立されている{{Cite web|和書| author = 千代田区観光協会 | title = 日本大学開校の地 | publisher = 千代田区観光協会 | date = | url = http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 日本大学 http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 | page= | quote = }} |- |後身校 | style="background:white;" |[[日本大学]] |} '''日本法律学校'''（にほんほうりつがっこう）は、[[1889年]]（[[明治]]22年）10月に[[東京市]][[麹町区]][[飯田橋|飯田町]]の[[皇典講究所]]内に設立設立認可。された[[私立学校|私立]][[法律学校 (旧制)|法律学校]]。[[大日本帝国憲法]]公布にともない、[[皇典講究所]]所長である[[法務大臣|司法大臣]][[山田顕義]]が、[[日本]]の[[法律]]を研究し国運の増進をはかる目的とする学校の設立をめざし、同じ趣旨で学校設立計画を進める法律学者らを全面的に支援して設立された。この項目では後身である日本大学（[[専門学校令]]準拠）についても扱う。 == 概要 == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|[[皇典講究所]]発祥記念碑]] 現在の'''[[日本大学]]の前身'''である私立法律学校である。現在の日大では本校の設立認可がなされた1889年10月4日を大学創立の日付とし、この日は同大学の「創立記念日」として継承されている 日本法律学校の設立認可からちょうど100年後の[[1989年]]（平成元年）10月4日には、[[上皇明仁|明仁天皇]]および[[上皇后美智子|美智子皇后]]の臨席のもと日本大学の創立百周年記念式典が挙行されている。{{Cite web|和書| author = 天皇・皇后| title = 主な式典におけるおことば（平成元年） | publisher = [[宮内庁]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。日大の学部・学科のうち[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]法律学科および[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|文理学部]]は「日本法律学校」時代に、法学部政治経済学科・[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]は[[専門学校令]]準拠時代（[[旧制専門学校]]としての日本大学時代）にまでその起源を遡ることができる。 [[1889年]]（明治22年）[[4月3日]]の「日本法律学校設立趣意書」の趣意では、「外来の先進ヨーロッパ諸国の法学思想とわが国固有の思想との融合調和を目指し、日本独自の法律文化を確立するため、法学教育の機関を創設すべき必要がある」とし、主意書に記されている創立目的を要約すると、「日本の法律は新旧を問わず学ぶ、海外の法律を参考として長所を取り入れる、日本法学という学問を提唱する」とした。[[近代国家]]の成立期、従来のように欧米法教育が主流の時代において、日本法律を教育する学校として誕生した本校は独自性を発揮することとなった。 開校当初は、[[皇典講究所]]の校舎を借り受けて授業を行うなど、同所および同所内に設立された[[國學院]]と深い関係を有していた。また設立当初行っていた夜間授業は最初に認可されたものである。 == 沿革 == === 設立時の経緯 === [[ファイル:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|学祖・[[山田顕義]]]] [[ファイル:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|創立者総代・[[宮崎道三郎]]]] [[ファイル:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|初代校長・[[金子堅太郎]]]] [[ファイル:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|第2代校長、初代総長・[[松岡康毅]]]] [[1889年]]（明治22年2月11日に[[大日本帝国憲法]]が発布されると、[[法学|法学界]]の中から'''外国の法理論は参考とし、日本の法律を中心に研究することを趣旨とする学校の設立'''を求める声が起こった。当時、初代[[法務大臣|司法大臣]]の任にあった[[山田顕義]]は、日本最初となるこの憲法の施行に向け日本独自の[[法典]]研究と教育が急務であると考え、自らが所長を兼ねていた[[皇典講究所]]内に「[[国法]]科」を新設することを構想した。また同時期、山田とは別に[[東京大学|東京帝国大学]]教授・[[宮崎道三郎]]を中心とする若手の法律学者らによって日本法律を教授する学校の設立の計画が進められていた。これらを契機として、山田は宮崎や憲法起草者である[[金子堅太郎]]ら法学者11名と協議し、新たな理念と思想を持つ法律学校設立のための設立要旨を次のように取りまとめた。 「一、国法は日本固有の国体・民情・慣習・ 文化を根底として作らるべきであり，この際日本古来の慣習制度をみ直す　二、憲法はじめ法律が多数制定されつつある現在，これを国民に熟知徹底させるために日本法律を講義する　三、日本法律として成立した法律を検討し，古来の精神・慣習・制度の面から必要な改正の議をたてる　四、同時に海外の法理もまた大いに研究し，わが国法学に資し，もって日本法学を振起して国運の増進をはかる」。 上記の設立要旨をもって1889年9月、[[東京府]]に設立許可が申請され、同年10月4日に設立が認可された日本法律学校は、翌年の[[1890年]]9月、設立者の一人である金子堅太郎を初代校長に迎えて開校した。開校当初、本校は皇典講究所の校舎内に設置され、同所の校舎（教室）を夜間借り受けて講義を行なう形式をとっていたが、これは同じ年の1890年、皇典講究所内に国史・国文・国法を教授する[[國學院]]が開校したことにともない、当初の山田の構想に沿って同校において国法を専修し法典研究にあたる部局として位置づけられていたためである{{Cite web|和書| author = | title = 学部・学科等の理念・目的 - 國學院大學 | publisher = | date = | url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf | accessdate = 2016-02-23 | page= 6 | quote =}}。 一方、設立評議員となった山田顕義は、設立時に示した開学理念による思想的影響に止まらず、運営財政面を中心にさまざまな形で本校の設立事業とその後の学校の発展に大きく貢献した。彼の支援によって設立時には[[司法省 (日本)|司法省]]から「法律取調事業嘱託費」の名目で50,000円の下付がなされただけでなく、設立後にも彼は[[文部省]]に対して「特別認可学校」とするよう要請を行った。さらに彼はさまざまな近代法典編纂に関わり日本における「近代法の祖」と称されていることから、本校の後身機関である日本大学は彼に「'''学祖'''」の称号を与え、大学の歴史上特別な位置づけとしている。 === 皇典講究所からの独立 === [[1892年]]11月11日、庇護者である山田が死去すると資金難が予想されたため本学は廃校も協議されるようになり、卒業生46名を送り出した[[1893年]]7月の第1回卒業式の直前には金子校長が辞職する事態となった。しかし卒業生の運動もあって本学はこの危機を乗り切り、1893年12月には[[司法省 (日本)#指定学校|司法省指定学校]]とされ[[松岡康毅]]が第2代校長に就任し、学校経営を安定させることに成功した。そして[[1897年]]には学術研究の機関誌として『日本法政新誌』が創刊されるなど、法律学校としての体裁も次第に整備された。これらと並行して[[1895年]]～[[1896年]]の校地移転、および1896年12月の[[財団法人]]改組を通じて皇典講究所からの組織的独立も果たした。 === 「日本大学」と改称 === 当初法律学科現在の[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|日大法学部]]法律学科の前身。のみを設置していた本学は、[[1901年]]10月に[[高等師範学校|高等師範科]]現在の[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|日大文理学部]]の前身。を設置して単なる法律学校に止まらない[[総合大学]]への昇格を目指すようになり、[[1903年]]8月、'''[[日本大学]]と改称'''し、翌[[1904年]]に[[専門学校令]]準拠の高等教育機関となり、併せて大学部に政治科・商科それぞれ現在の法学部政治経済学科、および[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]の前身。を併設した。 なお、校名を日本法律学校から日本大学に改めることに[[文部省]]は難色を示し、理事の[[戸水寛人]]を呼びつけて「日本法律学校なら日本の法律を教える学校なので問題ないが、日本大学だと[[大日本帝国|日本]]を代表する[[旧官立大学|国立大学]]と間違えられる恐れがある」として再考を求めた。しかし戸水は承服せず、「日本大学が駄目なら[[日本学園中学校・高等学校|日本中学]]はどうなるのか」と主張し、ついに日本大学への改称を認めさせたというエピソードが知られている[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ 日本大学への改称に尽力 戸水 寛人｜日本大学の歴史][[河岡潮風]] 『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 東都游学学校評判記]』 [[博文館]]、1909年、143-144頁『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、497-498頁。 === 大学昇格への道 === この時点では制度上[[旧制専門学校]]であった日本大学が[[大学令]]による制度上の大学（[[旧制大学]]）に昇格したのは、[[1920年]]（大正9年）4月16日である。そして、専門学校令準拠の日本大学は在籍者の卒業を待って1922年度いっぱいで廃止された『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、77頁。 == 年表 == [[File:日本法律学校（1896年頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|日本法律学校（1896年頃）]] [[File:1912年（明治45年）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|1912年改築の校舎]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|三崎町校舎（1920年竣工）]] * [[1889年]]（明治22年） ** 9月 - [[東京府]]に日本法律学校の設立許可が申請される。 ** 10月4日 -''' 設立認可'''。 * [[1890年]]（明治23年）9月 - 金子堅太郎を初代校長として開校式挙行。 * [[1893年]]（明治26年） ** 7月16日 - 第1回卒業生46名。 ** 12月 - 司法省指定学校となり判事検事登用試験の受験資格が与えられる。 *[[1895年]]（明治28年）- 校舎を大日本教育会（[[神田区]][[一ツ橋]]通）内に移転。 *[[1897年]]（明治30年）1月 - 学術研究誌『'''日本法政新誌'''』第1号が刊行。 *[[1898年]]（明治31年）12月22日 - [[財団法人]]組織に改組し、皇典講究所から組織的独立当時、[[財団法人]]化にしたのは本校が最初である。。 * [[1901年]]（明治34年）10月 - 高等師範科設置。 * [[1903年]]（明治36年） ** 2月 - 高等予備科・高等法学科を設置。 ** 8月19日 - [[校則]]を改め'''大学組織「日本大学」に改称'''。記念して徽章と制服・制帽を制定。 ** 12月 - 外国語専修部（英語・ドイツ語専修科）を設置。 * [[1904年]]（明治37年） ** 3月 - [[専門学校令]]準拠の[[旧制専門学校]]となり、従前の大学部法律学科と並んで政治科・商科を併設。 ** 10月 - 大学部法律学科・政治科・商科に在籍する学生総数は1,800名、教員総数約80名であった。 * [[1905年]]（明治38年）10月 - 大学部商科の授業開始『日本大学商学部百年史』 69頁。 * [[1911年]]（明治44年）4月 - 大学部・専門部の政治科の授業開始『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、508-510頁。 * [[1917年]]（大正{{0}}6年）4月 - 予科の[[修業年限]]を2年に延長。 * [[1920年]]（大正{{0}}9年）4月16日 - '''[[大学令]]準拠の[[旧制大学|（旧制）大学]]として発足'''。法文学部（法律科・政治科・宗教科・社会科）と商学部（商科）を設置。 * [[1923年]]（大正12年）3月 - 専門学校令準拠の大学部・大学予科を廃止。 == 創立に関わった人物 == 日本大学の「学祖」とされる山田顕義が創立に深く関わっている。 === 設立評議員 === * [[山田顕義]] * [[箕作麟祥]] * [[加藤弘之]] * [[穂積八束]] * [[児島惟謙]] * [[松岡康毅]] * [[清浦奎吾]] * [[中村元嘉]] === 創立者 === * [[宮崎道三郎]]（創立者総代） * [[金子堅太郎]]（初代校長） * [[樋山資之]]（幹事） * [[斯波淳六郎]]（幹事） * [[野田藤吉郎]]（幹事） * [[本多康直]] * [[末岡精一]] * [[添田寿一]] * [[穂積八束]] * [[平島及平]] * [[上條慎蔵]] == 歴代校長・学長・総長 == * 初代：[[金子堅太郎]]（[[1890年]]10月～[[1893年]]7月） * 第2代：[[松岡康毅]]（1893年12月～[[1923年]]9月）[[1903年]]8月に専門学校令準拠の日本大学学長、[[1920年]]4月に大学令準拠の日本大学学長、[[1922年]]3月に総長となった。 == 校地の変遷と継承 == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|日本大学開校の地（[[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）]] 設立時の校地は、先述の通り皇典講究所のあった[[東京市]]'''[[麹町区]]飯田町'''（現在の[[東京都]][[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）に所在し、木造2階建ての校舎を昼は國學院が、夜は日本法律学校が使用していた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、336-337頁。 山田没後の[[1895年]]（明治28年）10月に[[神田区]][[一ツ橋|一ツ橋通町]]（現・[[千代田区]][[一ツ橋]]2丁目）の[[大日本教育会]]内の一室を借りて移転したが、間もなく大日本教育会に合併話が持ち上がり、教室の継続使用ができなくなったため、翌年6月[[神田区]][[神田三崎町|三崎町]]3丁目の練兵場跡地の校舎に移転して皇典講究所から独立した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、401-406頁。当初の敷地は約220坪、建坪は約160坪。3つの教室と講師室、事務室などが設けられていたに過ぎなかったが、明治30年代には増築を重ねて6部屋の教室を擁する2階建て校舎となり『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、409頁、[[1912年]]（明治45年）にも改築の手が加えられた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695頁。 [[1918年]]（大正7年）には創立30周年記念事業の一環として新校舎の建設構想が浮上した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695-702頁。[[大学令]]による認可条件として施設整備は必須だったため、[[1919年]]（大正8年）12月に起工、認可間もない[[1920年]]（大正9年）5月に新校舎落成式、大正8年度卒業式、校友大会を兼ねた昇格祝賀会を行った『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、87-96頁。 三崎町校舎は現在の日本大学神田三崎町キャンパス（[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]および両学部管轄の大学院研究科が所在）に継承されている。旧飯田町校舎の所在地は現在、'''「日本大学開校の地」の碑'''が建立されている{{Cite web|和書| author = 千代田区観光協会 | title = 日本大学開校の地 | publisher = 千代田区観光協会 | date = | url = http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 日本大学 {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |Nihon Law School |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |[[1889]] [[October 4]]
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |[[Tokyo City]] [[Kōjimachi Ward]] (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |[[Miyazaki Michisaburō]]{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |[[Nihon University]] |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private [[law school]] established in October [[1889]] (Meiji 22) within the [[Kōten Kōkyūjo]] in [[Iidamachi]], [[Kōjimachi Ward]], [[Tokyo City]].Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the [[Constitution of the Empire of Japan]], [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese [[law]] to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, [[Nihon University]] (in compliance with the [[Specialized School Order]]). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of [[Kōten Kōkyūjo]]]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''[[Nihon University]]'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the Faculty of Law's Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the [[Kokugakuin]] established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. == History == === Circumstances at the Time of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|School Founder: [[Yamada Akiyoshi]]]] [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]]]] [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: [[Kaneko Kentarō]]]] [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: [[Matsuoka Kōki]]]] When the [[Constitution of the Empire of Japan]] was promulgated on February 11, 1889 (Meiji 22), voices arose from the [[legal community]] seeking the establishment of a school with the purpose of "referring to foreign legal theories but focusing on the study of Japanese law." At that time, [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], who was serving as the first Minister of Justice, considered that the study and education of uniquely Japanese [[legal codes]] were urgent in preparation for the enforcement of this first constitution in Japan. He conceived the idea of establishing a "National Law Department" within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, of which he was also the director. Around the same time, independently of Yamada, young legal scholars led by [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]], a professor at the [[University of Tokyo]], were advancing plans to establish a school that teaches Japanese law. Triggered by these events, Yamada consulted with eleven legal scholars including Miyazaki and [[Kaneko Kentarō]], a drafter of the constitution, and formulated the establishment outline for the new school with the following points: "1. National law should be created based on Japan's inherent national character, customs, and culture, and at this time, we should review Japan's ancient customs and institutions. 2. Currently, with many laws including the constitution being enacted, we should teach Japanese law to ensure that it is well understood by the people. 3. Examine the laws established as Japanese law, and propose necessary revisions from the perspectives of ancient spirit, customs, and institutions. 4. At the same time, extensively study foreign legal theories to contribute to our country's jurisprudence and promote Japanese legal studies to enhance national prosperity." With the above establishment outline, an application for permission to establish Nihon Law School was submitted to the [[Tokyo Prefecture]] in September 1889, and the establishment was approved on October 4 of the same year. The school opened in September of the following year, 1890, welcoming one of its founders, Kaneko Kentarō, as the first principal. At the time of opening, the school was set up within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms (classrooms) of the institute at night. This was because, in the same year 1890, with the opening of the [[Kokugakuin]] established within the Kōten Kōkyūjo to teach national history, national literature, and national law, the school was positioned, in line with Yamada's initial concept, as a department specializing in national law within Kokugakuin to engage in the study of legal codes.{{Cite web|Japanese book| title = Philosophy and Purpose of Faculties and Departments - Kokugakuin University | url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf | accessdate = 2016-02-23 | page= 6 }} On the other hand, Yamada Akiyoshi, who became an establishment councilor, not only influenced the school's founding philosophy at the time of establishment but also made significant contributions to the establishment project and the subsequent development of the school in various ways, mainly in terms of operational finance. With his support, not only was a subsidy of 50,000 yen granted from the [[Ministry of Justice]] at the time of establishment under the name of "Legal Investigation Project Commission Expenses", but after the establishment, he also requested the [[Ministry of Education]] to designate the school as a "Specially Approved School". Furthermore, since he was involved in various modern legal code compilations and is called the "Father of Modern Law" in Japan, Nihon University, the successor institution of this school, has given him the title of "'''School Founder'''" and places him in a special position in the university's history. === Independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo === When Yamada, the patron, passed away on November 11, 1892, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the school even discussed closure. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July 1893, which saw 46 graduates, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, the school overcame this crisis partly due to the efforts of the graduates, and in December 1893, it was designated as a school approved by the Ministry of Justice, and [[Matsuoka Kōki]] became the second principal, succeeding in stabilizing the school's management. In 1897, the academic journal "'''Nihon Hōsei Shinshi'''" was launched as a research organ, and the school's structure as a law school was gradually improved. Parallel to these developments, through the relocation of the campus in 1895-1896 and the reorganization into a [[foundation]] in December 1896, the school also achieved organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renamed to "Nihon University" === Initially, the school only had a Department of LawThe predecessor of the Department of Law in the current [[Nihon University College of Law]]., but in October 1901, it established a Higher Normal DepartmentThe predecessor of the current [[Nihon University College of Humanities and Sciences]]. and began aiming to become a comprehensive university beyond just a law school. In August 1903, it was renamed '''[[Nihon University]]''', and in the following year, 1904, it became a higher education institution under the [[Specialized School Order]], and concurrently established the Departments of Politics and CommerceThese are the predecessors of the Department of Political Science and Economics in the Faculty of Law, and the current [[Nihon University College of Commerce]] and [[Nihon University College of Economics]]. in the university division. It should be noted that the Ministry of Education showed reluctance to change the school name from Nihon Law School to Nihon University. They summoned director [[Tomizu Hirondo]] and requested reconsideration, saying, "If it's Nihon Law School, there's no problem since it's a school that teaches Japanese law, but if it's Nihon University, there's a risk of being mistaken for a national university representing Japan." However, Tomizu did not agree, arguing, "If Nihon University is not allowed, what about [[Nihon Gakuen Junior and Senior High School|Nihon Middle School]]?" and eventually got approval to rename the school to Nihon University.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Tomizu Hirondo's Efforts to Rename to Nihon University | History of Nihon University]Kawaoka Chōfū, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Tōto Yūgaku Gakkō Hyōbanki]" Hakubunkan, 1909, pp. 143-144"Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 497-498 === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University, which was institutionally a specialized school, was elevated to a university under the [[University Ordinance]] (as an old system university) on April 16, 1920 (Taishō 9). The Nihon University under the Specialized School Order was abolished at the end of the 1922 academic year after waiting for the graduation of enrolled students."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 2, p. 77 == Timeline == [[File:日本法律学校（1896年頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (around 1896)]] [[File:1912年（明治45年）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|School building renovated in 1912]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Misakichō Campus (completed in 1920)]] * [[1889]] (Meiji 22) * September - Application for permission to establish Nihon Law School submitted to [[Tokyo Prefecture]]. * October 4 - '''Establishment approved'''. * [[1890]] (Meiji 23) September - Opening ceremony held with Kaneko Kentarō as the first principal. * [[1893]] (Meiji 26) * July 16 - First graduation ceremony with 46 graduates. * December - Designated as a school approved by the Ministry of Justice, granting eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor appointment examinations. * [[1895]] (Meiji 28) - Relocated campus to within the [[Dai-Nippon Educational Association]] (Kanda-ku Hitotsubashi Street). * [[1897]] (Meiji 30) January - First issue of the academic journal "'''Nihon Hōsei Shinshi'''" published. * [[1898]] (Meiji 31) December 22 - Reorganized into a [[foundation]], achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo.At the time, this school was the first to become a foundation. * [[1901]] (Meiji 34) October - Established Higher Normal Department. * [[1903]] (Meiji 36) * February - Established Higher Preparatory Course and Higher Law Course. * August 19 - '''Renamed to "Nihon University"''' by revising the school regulations. Commemoratively established badges, uniforms, and caps. * December - Established Foreign Language Specialized Department (English and German Specialized Courses). * [[1904]] (Meiji 37) * March - Became an [[old system specialized school]] under the [[Specialized School Order]], and alongside the existing University Division's Department of Law, established the Departments of Politics and Commerce. * October - The total number of students enrolled in the University Division's Departments of Law, Politics, and Commerce was 1,800, and the total number of faculty was about 80. * [[1905]] (Meiji 38) October - Classes began for the University Division's Department of Commerce."Nihon University College of Commerce Centennial History" p. 69 * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) April - Classes began for the University Division and Specialized Division's Departments of Politics."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 508-510 * [[1917]] (Taishō 6) April - Extended the course duration of the Preparatory Course to two years. * [[1920]] (Taishō 9) April 16 - '''Established as a university under the [[University Ordinance]]''' (as an old system university). Established the College of Law and Literature (Departments of Law, Politics, Religion, and Society) and the College of Commerce (Department of Commerce). * [[1923]] (Taishō 12) March - Abolished the University Division and University Preparatory Course under the Specialized School Order. == People Involved in the Founding == [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], regarded as the "School Founder" of Nihon University, was deeply involved in the establishment. === Establishment Councilors === * [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] * [[Mitsukuri Rinshō]] * [[Katō Hiroyuki]] * [[Hozumi Yatsuka]] * [[Kojima Iken]] * [[Matsuoka Kōki]] * [[Kiyoura Keigo]] * [[Nakamura Motoyoshi]] === Founders === * [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]] (Chief Founder) * [[Kaneko Kentarō]] (First Principal) * [[Hiyama Sukeyuki]] (Executive) * [[Shiba Jūrōkurō]] (Executive) * [[Noda Tōkichirō]] (Executive) * [[Honda Yasunao]] * [[Sueoka Seiichi]] * [[Soeda Juichi]] * [[Hozumi Yatsuka]] * [[Hirashima Kyūhei]] * [[Kamijō Shinzō]] == Successive Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First Principal: [[Kaneko Kentarō]] (October 1890 – July 1893) * Second Principal: [[Matsuoka Kōki]] (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, became President of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order; in April 1920, became President of Nihon University under the University Ordinance; in March 1922, became Chancellor. == Transition and Continuation of the Campus == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Place of Nihon University's opening (Iidabashi, [[Chiyoda Ward]])]] As mentioned earlier, the campus at the time of establishment was located within the Kōten Kōkyūjo in '''Iidamachi''', [[Kōjimachi Ward]], [[Tokyo City]] (currently [[Iidabashi]], [[Chiyoda Ward]], [[Tokyo]]), and the school shared a two-story wooden building with Kokugakuin, using the classrooms during the day and Nihon Law School at night."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 336-337 In October 1895 (Meiji 28), after the death of Yamada, the school moved to a room within the [[Dai-Nippon Educational Association]] in Hitotsubashi-dōri, [[Kanda Ward]] (now Hitotsubashi 2-chome, Chiyoda Ward). However, soon after, a merger with the Dai-Nippon Educational Association was proposed, and since continued use of the classrooms became impossible, the school relocated in June of the following year to a campus on the site of a former training ground in 3-chome, Misakichō, Kanda Ward, achieving independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 401-406 The initial site was about 220 tsubo (approx. 727 square meters), and the building area was about 160 tsubo (approx. 529 square meters). There were only three classrooms, a lecturer's room, and an office, but in the 1890s, it was expanded several times to become a two-story building with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, p. 409 In 1912 (Meiji 45), further renovations were made."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, p. 695 In 1918 (Taishō 7), as part of the 30th-anniversary commemorative project, plans for constructing a new school building emerged."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 695-702 Since facility improvement was essential as a condition for approval under the University Ordinance, construction began in December 1919 (Taishō 8), and shortly after approval, in May 1920 (Taishō 9), a ceremony was held to celebrate the completion of the new school building, the graduation ceremony for the Taishō 8 academic year, and a celebration of the university's elevation."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 2, pp. 87-96 The Misakichō campus has been inherited by the current Nihon University Kanda Misakichō Campus (where the [[Nihon University College of Law]] and [[Nihon University College of Economics]] and their respective graduate schools are located). A monument titled '''"Place of Nihon University's Opening"''' has been erected at the site of the former Iidamachi campus.{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Chiyoda City Tourism Association | title = Place of Nihon University's Opening | publisher = Chiyoda City Tourism Association | url = http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == However, the school overcame this crisis partly due to the efforts of the graduates, and in December 1893, it was designated as a school approved by the Ministry of Justice, and [[Matsuoka Kōki]] became the second principal, succeeding in stabilizing the school's management. In 1897, the academic journal "'''Nihon Hōsei Shinshi'''" was launched as a research organ, and the school's structure as a law school was gradually improved. Parallel to these developments, through the relocation of the campus in 1895-1896 and the reorganization into a [[foundation]] in December 1896, the school also achieved organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renamed to "Nihon University" === Initially, the school only had a Department of LawThe predecessor of the Department of Law in the current [[Nihon University College of Law]]., but in October 1901, it established a Higher Normal DepartmentThe predecessor of the current [[Nihon University College of Humanities and Sciences]]. and began aiming to become a comprehensive university beyond just a law school. In August 1903, it was renamed '''[[Nihon University]]''', and in the following year, 1904, it became a higher education institution under the [[Specialized School Order]], and concurrently established the Departments of Politics and CommerceThese are the predecessors of the Department of Political Science and Economics in the Faculty of Law, and the current [[Nihon University College of Commerce]] and [[Nihon University College of Economics]]. in the university division. It should be noted that the Ministry of Education showed reluctance to change the school name from Nihon Law School to Nihon University. They summoned director [[Tomizu Hirondo]] and requested reconsideration, saying, "If it's Nihon Law School, there's no problem since it's a school that teaches Japanese law, but if it's Nihon University, there's a risk of being mistaken for a national university representing Japan." However, Tomizu did not agree, arguing, "If Nihon University is not allowed, what about [[Nihon Gakuen Junior and Senior High School|Nihon Middle School]]?" and eventually got approval to rename the school to Nihon University.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Tomizu Hirondo's Efforts to Rename to Nihon University | History of Nihon University]Kawaoka Chōfū, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Tōto Yūgaku Gakkō Hyōbanki]" Hakubunkan, 1909, pp. 143-144"Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 497-498 === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University, which was institutionally a specialized school, was elevated to a university under the [[University Ordinance]] (as an old system university) on April 16, 1920 (Taishō 9). The Nihon University under the Specialized School Order was abolished at the end of the 1922 academic year after waiting for the graduation of enrolled students."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 2, p. 77 == Timeline == [[File:日本法律学校（1896年頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (around 1896)]] [[File:1912年（明治45年）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|School building renovated in 1912]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Misakichō Campus (completed in 1920)]] * [[1889]] (Meiji 22) * September - Application for permission to establish Nihon Law School submitted to [[Tokyo Prefecture]]. * October 4 - '''Establishment approved'''. * [[1890]] (Meiji 23) September - Opening ceremony held with Kaneko Kentarō as the first principal. * [[1893]] (Meiji 26) * July 16 - First graduation ceremony with 46 graduates. * December - Designated as a school approved by the Ministry of Justice, granting eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor appointment examinations. * [[1895]] (Meiji 28) - Relocated campus to within the [[Dai-Nippon Educational Association]] (Kanda-ku Hitotsubashi Street). * [[1897]] (Meiji 30) January - First issue of the academic journal "'''Nihon Hōsei Shinshi'''" published. * [[1898]] (Meiji 31) December 22 - Reorganized into a [[foundation]], achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo.At the time, this school was the first to become a foundation. * [[1901]] (Meiji 34) October - Established Higher Normal Department. * [[1903]] (Meiji 36) * February - Established Higher Preparatory Course and Higher Law Course. * August 19 - '''Renamed to "Nihon University"''' by revising the school regulations. Commemoratively established badges, uniforms, and caps. * December - Established Foreign Language Specialized Department (English and German Specialized Courses). * [[1904]] (Meiji 37) * March - Became an [[old system specialized school]] under the [[Specialized School Order]], and alongside the existing University Division's Department of Law, established the Departments of Politics and Commerce. * October - The total number of students enrolled in the University Division's Departments of Law, Politics, and Commerce was 1,800, and the total number of faculty was about 80. * [[1905]] (Meiji 38) October - Classes began for the University Division's Department of Commerce."Nihon University College of Commerce Centennial History" p. 69 * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) April - Classes began for the University Division and Specialized Division's Departments of Politics."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 508-510 * [[1917]] (Taishō 6) April - Extended the course duration of the Preparatory Course to two years. * [[1920]] (Taishō 9) April 16 - '''Established as a university under the [[University Ordinance]]''' (as an old system university). Established the College of Law and Literature (Departments of Law, Politics, Religion, and Society) and the College of Commerce (Department of Commerce). * [[1923]] (Taishō 12) March - Abolished the University Division and University Preparatory Course under the Specialized School Order. == People Involved in the Founding == [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], regarded as the "School Founder" of Nihon University, was deeply involved in the establishment. === Establishment Councilors === * [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] * [[Mitsukuri Rinshō]] * [[Katō Hiroyuki]] * [[Hozumi Yatsuka]] * [[Kojima Iken]] * [[Matsuoka Kōki]] * [[Kiyoura Keigo]] * [[Nakamura Motoyoshi]] === Founders === * [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]] (Chief Founder) * [[Kaneko Kentarō]] (First Principal) * [[Hiyama Sukeyuki]] (Executive) * [[Shiba Jūrōkurō]] (Executive) * [[Noda Tōkichirō]] (Executive) * [[Honda Yasunao]] * [[Sueoka Seiichi]] * [[Soeda Juichi]] * [[Hozumi Yatsuka]] * [[Hirashima Kyūhei]] * [[Kamijō Shinzō]] == Successive Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First Principal: [[Kaneko Kentarō]] (October 1890 – July 1893) * Second Principal: [[Matsuoka Kōki]] (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, became President of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order; in April 1920, became President of Nihon University under the University Ordinance; in March 1922, became Chancellor. == Transition and Continuation of the Campus == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Place of Nihon University's opening (Iidabashi, [[Chiyoda Ward]])]] As mentioned earlier, the campus at the time of establishment was located within the Kōten Kōkyūjo in '''Iidamachi''', [[Kōjimachi Ward]], [[Tokyo City]] (currently [[Iidabashi]], [[Chiyoda Ward]], [[Tokyo]]), and the school shared a two-story wooden building with Kokugakuin, using the classrooms during the day and Nihon Law School at night."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 336-337 In October 1895 (Meiji 28), after the death of Yamada, the school moved to a room within the [[Dai-Nippon Educational Association]] in Hitotsubashi-dōri, [[Kanda Ward]] (now Hitotsubashi 2-chome, Chiyoda Ward). However, soon after, a merger with the Dai-Nippon Educational Association was proposed, and since continued use of the classrooms became impossible, the school relocated in June of the following year to a campus on the site of a former training ground in 3-chome, Misakichō, Kanda Ward, achieving independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 401-406 The initial site was about 220 tsubo (approx. 727 square meters), and the building area was about 160 tsubo (approx. 529 square meters). There were only three classrooms, a lecturer's room, and an office, but in the 1890s, it was expanded several times to become a two-story building with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, p. 409 In 1912 (Meiji 45), further renovations were made."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, p. 695 In 1918 (Taishō 7), as part of the 30th-anniversary commemorative project, plans for constructing a new school building emerged."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 695-702 Since facility improvement was essential as a condition for approval under the University Ordinance, construction began in December 1919 (Taishō 8), and shortly after approval, in May 1920 (Taishō 9), a ceremony was held to celebrate the completion of the new school building, the graduation ceremony for the Taishō 8 academic year, and a celebration of the university's elevation."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 2, pp. 87-96 The Misakichō campus has been inherited by the current Nihon University Kanda Misakichō Campus (where the [[Nihon University College of Law]] and [[Nihon University College of Economics]] and their respective graduate schools are located). A monument titled '''"Place of Nihon University's Opening"''' has been erected at the site of the former Iidamachi campus.{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Chiyoda City Tourism Association | title = {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] [[ja:日本法律学校]] == History == === Circumstances at the Time of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|School Founder: [[Yamada Akiyoshi]]]] [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]]]] [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: [[Kaneko Kentarō]]]] [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: [[Matsuoka Kōki]]]] When the [[Constitution of the Empire of Japan]] was promulgated on February 11, 1889 (Meiji 22), voices arose from the [[legal community]] seeking the establishment of a school with the purpose of "referring to foreign legal theories but focusing on the study of Japanese law." At that time, [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], who was serving as the first Minister of Justice, considered that the study and education of uniquely Japanese [[legal codes]] were urgent in preparation for the enforcement of this first constitution in Japan. He conceived the idea of establishing a "National Law Department" within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, of which he was also the director. Around the same time, independently of Yamada, young legal scholars led by [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]], a professor at the [[University of Tokyo]], were advancing plans to establish a school that teaches Japanese law. Triggered by these events, Yamada consulted with eleven legal scholars including Miyazaki and [[Kaneko Kentarō]], a drafter of the constitution, and formulated the establishment outline for the new school with the following points: "1. National law should be created based on Japan's inherent national character, customs, and culture, and at this time, we should review Japan's ancient customs and institutions. 2. Currently, with many laws including the constitution being enacted, we should teach Japanese law to ensure that it is well understood by the people. 3. Examine the laws established as Japanese law, and propose necessary revisions from the perspectives of ancient spirit, customs, and institutions. 4. At the same time, extensively study foreign legal theories to contribute to our country's jurisprudence and promote Japanese legal studies to enhance national prosperity." With the above establishment outline, an application for permission to establish Nihon Law School was submitted to the [[Tokyo Prefecture]] in September 1889, and the establishment was approved on October 4 of the same year. The school opened in September of the following year, 1890, welcoming one of its founders, Kaneko Kentarō, as the first principal. At the time of opening, the school was set up within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms (classrooms) of the institute at night. This was because, in the same year 1890, with the opening of the [[Kokugakuin]] established within the Kōten Kōkyūjo to teach national history, national literature, and national law, the school was positioned, in line with Yamada's initial concept, as a department specializing in national law within Kokugakuin to engage in the study of legal codes.{{Cite web|Japanese book| title = Philosophy and Purpose of Faculties and Departments - Kokugakuin University | url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf | accessdate = 2016-02-23 | page= 6 }} On the other hand, Yamada Akiyoshi, who became an establishment councilor, not only influenced the school's founding philosophy at the time of establishment but also made significant contributions to the establishment project and the subsequent development of the school in various ways, mainly in terms of operational finance. With his support, not only was a subsidy of 50,000 yen granted from the [[Ministry of Justice]] at the time of establishment under the name of "Legal Investigation Project Commission Expenses", but after the establishment, he also requested the [[Ministry of Education]] to designate the school as a "Specially Approved School". Furthermore, since he was involved in various modern legal code compilations and is called the "Father of Modern Law" in Japan, Nihon University, the successor institution of this school, has given him the title of "'''School Founder'''" and places him in a special position in the university's history. === Independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo === When Yamada, the patron, passed away on November 11, 1892, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the school even discussed closure. A monument titled '''"Place of Nihon University's Opening"''' has been erected at the site of the former Iidamachi campus.{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Chiyoda City Tourism Association | title = {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] [[ja:日本法律学校]] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}]] [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}]] [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}]] [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}}]] In {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892年}}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893年}}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897年}}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895年}} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896年}}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901年}},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903年}}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920年}}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922年}} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Timeline == [[File:日本法律学校（1896年頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (around 1896)]] [[File:1912年（明治45年）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|School building renovated in 1912]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Misakichō Campus (completed in 1920)]] * [[1889]] (Meiji 22) * September - Application for permission to establish Nihon Law School submitted to [[Tokyo Prefecture]]. * October 4 - '''Establishment approved'''. * [[1890]] (Meiji 23) September - Opening ceremony held with Kaneko Kentarō as the first principal. * [[1893]] (Meiji 26) * July 16 - First graduation ceremony with 46 graduates. * December - Designated as a school approved by the Ministry of Justice, granting eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor appointment examinations. * [[1895]] (Meiji 28) - Relocated campus to within the [[Dai-Nippon Educational Association]] (Kanda-ku Hitotsubashi Street). * [[1897]] (Meiji 30) January - First issue of the academic journal "'''Nihon Hōsei Shinshi'''" published. * [[1898]] (Meiji 31) December 22 - Reorganized into a [[foundation]], achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo.At the time, this school was the first to become a foundation. * [[1901]] (Meiji 34) October - Established Higher Normal Department. * [[1903]] (Meiji 36) * February - Established Higher Preparatory Course and Higher Law Course. * August 19 - '''Renamed to "Nihon University"''' by revising the school regulations. Commemoratively established badges, uniforms, and caps. * December - Established Foreign Language Specialized Department (English and German Specialized Courses). * [[1904]] (Meiji 37) * March - Became an [[old system specialized school]] under the [[Specialized School Order]], and alongside the existing University Division's Department of Law, established the Departments of Politics and Commerce. * October - The total number of students enrolled in the University Division's Departments of Law, Politics, and Commerce was 1,800, and the total number of faculty was about 80. * [[1905]] (Meiji 38) October - Classes began for the University Division's Department of Commerce."Nihon University College of Commerce Centennial History" p. 69 * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) April - Classes began for the University Division and Specialized Division's Departments of Politics."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 508-510 * [[1917]] (Taishō 6) April - Extended the course duration of the Preparatory Course to two years. * [[1920]] (Taishō 9) April 16 - '''Established as a university under the [[University Ordinance]]''' (as an old system university). Established the College of Law and Literature (Departments of Law, Politics, Religion, and Society) and the College of Commerce (Department of Commerce). * [[1923]] (Taishō 12) March - Abolished the University Division and University Preparatory Course under the Specialized School Order. == People Involved in the Founding == [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], regarded as the "School Founder" of Nihon University, was deeply involved in the establishment. === Establishment Councilors === * [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] * [[Mitsukuri Rinshō]] * [[Katō Hiroyuki]] * [[Hozumi Yatsuka]] * [[Kojima Iken]] * [[Matsuoka Kōki]] * [[Kiyoura Keigo]] * [[Nakamura Motoyoshi]] === Founders === * [[Miyazaki Michisaburō]] (Chief Founder) * [[Kaneko Kentarō]] (First Principal) * [[Hiyama Sukeyuki]] (Executive) * [[Shiba Jūrōkurō]] (Executive) * [[Noda Tōkichirō]] (Executive) * [[Honda Yasunao]] * [[Sueoka Seiichi]] * [[Soeda Juichi]] * [[Hozumi Yatsuka]] * [[Hirashima Kyūhei]] * [[Kamijō Shinzō]] == Successive Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First Principal: [[Kaneko Kentarō]] (October 1890 – July 1893) * Second Principal: [[Matsuoka Kōki]] (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, became President of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order; in April 1920, became President of Nihon University under the University Ordinance; in March 1922, became Chancellor. == Transition and Continuation of the Campus == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Place of Nihon University's opening (Iidabashi, [[Chiyoda Ward]])]] As mentioned earlier, the campus at the time of establishment was located within the Kōten Kōkyūjo in '''Iidamachi''', [[Kōjimachi Ward]], [[Tokyo City]] (currently [[Iidabashi]], [[Chiyoda Ward]], [[Tokyo]]), and the school shared a two-story wooden building with Kokugakuin, using the classrooms during the day and Nihon Law School at night."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 336-337 In October 1895 (Meiji 28), after the death of Yamada, the school moved to a room within the [[Dai-Nippon Educational Association]] in Hitotsubashi-dōri, [[Kanda Ward]] (now Hitotsubashi 2-chome, Chiyoda Ward). However, soon after, a merger with the Dai-Nippon Educational Association was proposed, and since continued use of the classrooms became impossible, the school relocated in June of the following year to a campus on the site of a former training ground in 3-chome, Misakichō, Kanda Ward, achieving independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 401-406 The initial site was about 220 tsubo (approx. 727 square meters), and the building area was about 160 tsubo (approx. 529 square meters). There were only three classrooms, a lecturer's room, and an office, but in the 1890s, it was expanded several times to become a two-story building with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, p. 409 In 1912 (Meiji 45), further renovations were made."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, p. 695 In 1918 (Taishō 7), as part of the 30th-anniversary commemorative project, plans for constructing a new school building emerged."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 1, pp. 695-702 Since facility improvement was essential as a condition for approval under the University Ordinance, construction began in December 1919 (Taishō 8), and shortly after approval, in May 1920 (Taishō 9), a ceremony was held to celebrate the completion of the new school building, the graduation ceremony for the Taishō 8 academic year, and a celebration of the university's elevation."Nihon University Centennial History" Vol. 2, pp. 87-96 The Misakichō campus has been inherited by the current Nihon University Kanda Misakichō Campus (where the [[Nihon University College of Law]] and [[Nihon University College of Economics]] and their respective graduate schools are located).
