{| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[ja:日本法律学校]] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year }}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year }}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year }},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year }}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year }}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year }} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. Courses in the Political Science Department began in both the university and specialized divisions."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 508–510. * {{ill|1917|ja|1917th year }} (Taisho 6) ''' April - Duration of the Preparatory Course extended to two years. * {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }} (Taisho 9) ''' April 16 * '''Reorganized as a university''' under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, establishing the Faculty of Arts and Letters (Departments of Law, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology) and the Faculty of Commerce (Commerce Department). * {{ill|1923|ja|1923rd year }} (Taisho 12) ''' March - University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year }} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year }}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year }}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year }}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[ja:日本法律学校]] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year }}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year }}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year }},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year }}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year }}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year }} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. Courses in the Political Science Department began in both the university and specialized divisions."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 508–510. * {{ill|1917|ja|1917th year }} (Taisho 6) ''' April - Duration of the Preparatory Course extended to two years. * {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }} (Taisho 9) ''' April 16 * '''Reorganized as a university''' under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, establishing the Faculty of Arts and Letters (Departments of Law, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology) and the Faculty of Commerce (Commerce Department). * {{ill|1923|ja|1923rd year }} (Taisho 12) ''' March - University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year }} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year }}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year }}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year }}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism Association|url=http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx|accessdate=March 2, 2016}} == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == * Nihon University [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/9580649 "Brief History of Nihon University in Seventy Years"] 1959 * Nihon University Centennial History Editorial Committee, "Nihon University Centennial History" Volumes 1-5, Nihon University, 1997-2006. * Nihon University Public Relations Department University History Editing Section, "Nihon University's Progress" Volumes 1-3, Nihon University, 2011. * {{Cite book|Japanese book|author=Murai {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[ja:日本法律学校]] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year }}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year }}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year }},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year }}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year }}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year }} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. ''' October 4 * '''Official recognition''' granted. * {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year }} (Meiji 23) ''' September - Opening ceremony held with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} as the first principal. * {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }} (Meiji 26) ''' July 16 - First graduating class of 46 students. ''' December - Designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting eligibility for judicial and prosecutorial examinations. * {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }} (Meiji 28) ''' Campus relocated to the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}, Ichibashi Street. * {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year }} (Meiji 30) ''' January - The first issue of the academic journal, "'''{{ill|Nihon Hosei Shinshi|ja|日本法政新誌}}'''," published. * {{ill|1898|ja|1898th year }} (Meiji 31) ''' December 22 - Reorganized as a {{ill|Public Interest Incorporated Foundation|ja|財団法人}} and achieved organizational independence from {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}.This school was the first to adopt the foundation system at the time. * {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year }} (Meiji 34) ''' October - Higher Normal Department established. * {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year }} (Meiji 36) ''' February - Preparatory and Advanced Law Departments established. ''' August 19 - Renamed to '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. In celebration, an official emblem and uniforms were introduced. ''' December - Department of Foreign Language Studies (English and German) established. * {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year }} (Meiji 37) ''' March - Reorganized under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}} as an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}, with Political Science and Commerce Departments added to the Law Department. ''' October - Total enrollment in the Law, Political Science, and Commerce Departments reached 1,800, with approximately 80 instructors. * {{ill|1905|ja|1905th year }} (Meiji 38) ''' October - Courses in the Commerce Department commenced."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 69. * {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year }} (Meiji 44) ''' April - Courses in the Political Science Department began in both the university and specialized divisions."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 508–510. * {{ill|1917|ja|1917th year }} (Taisho 6) ''' April - Duration of the Preparatory Course extended to two years. * {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }} (Taisho 9) ''' April 16 * '''Reorganized as a university''' under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, establishing the Faculty of Arts and Letters (Departments of Law, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology) and the Faculty of Commerce (Commerce Department). * {{ill|1923|ja|1923rd year }} (Taisho 12) ''' March - University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year }} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year }}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year }}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year }}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]][[sn:Japan Law School]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Japan Law School}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Japan Law School]][[ja:日本法律学校]] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year }}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year }}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year }},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year }}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year }}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year }} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year }} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. Courses in the Political Science Department began in both the university and specialized divisions."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 508–510. * {{ill|1917|ja|1917th year }} (Taisho 6) ''' April - Duration of the Preparatory Course extended to two years. * {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }} (Taisho 9) ''' April 16 * '''Reorganized as a university''' under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, establishing the Faculty of Arts and Letters (Departments of Law, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology) and the Faculty of Commerce (Commerce Department). * {{ill|1923|ja|1923rd year }} (Taisho 12) ''' March - University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year }} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year }}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year }}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year }}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year }}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year }}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year }}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year }}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism Association|url=http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx|accessdate=March 2, 2016}} == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == * Nihon University [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/9580649 "Brief History of Nihon University in Seventy Years"] 1959 * Nihon University Centennial History Editorial Committee, "Nihon University Centennial History" Volumes 1-5, Nihon University, 1997-2006. * Nihon
