{| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year}}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year}}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year}}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year}},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year}}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year}}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year}} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. ''' December - Designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting eligibility for judicial and prosecutorial examinations. * {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}} (Meiji 28) ''' Campus relocated to the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}, Ichibashi Street. * {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year}} (Meiji 30) ''' January - The first issue of the academic journal, "'''{{ill|Nihon Hosei Shinshi|ja|日本法政新誌}}'''," published. * {{ill|1898|ja|1898th year}} (Meiji 31) ''' December 22 - Reorganized as a {{ill|Public Interest Incorporated Foundation|ja|財団法人}} and achieved organizational independence from {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}.This school was the first to adopt the foundation system at the time. * {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year}} (Meiji 34) ''' October - Higher Normal Department established. * {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year}} (Meiji 36) ''' February - Preparatory and Advanced Law Departments established. University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year}} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year}}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year}}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |{{ill|Nihon Law School|ja|日本法律学校}} |- |Founded | style="background:white;" |{{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} {{ill|October 4|ja|10月4日}}
(Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year}}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year}}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year}}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year}},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year}}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year}}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year}} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. ''' October 4 * '''Official recognition''' granted. * {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year}} (Meiji 23) ''' September - Opening ceremony held with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} as the first principal. * {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}} (Meiji 26) ''' July 16 - First graduating class of 46 students. ''' December - Designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting eligibility for judicial and prosecutorial examinations. * {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}} (Meiji 28) ''' Campus relocated to the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}, Ichibashi Street. * {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year}} (Meiji 30) ''' January - The first issue of the academic journal, "'''{{ill|Nihon Hosei Shinshi|ja|日本法政新誌}}'''," published. * {{ill|1898|ja|1898th year}} (Meiji 31) ''' December 22 - Reorganized as a {{ill|Public Interest Incorporated Foundation|ja|財団法人}} and achieved organizational independence from {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}.This school was the first to adopt the foundation system at the time. * {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year}} (Meiji 34) ''' October - Higher Normal Department established. * {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year}} (Meiji 36) ''' February - Preparatory and Advanced Law Departments established. ''' August 19 - Renamed to '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. In celebration, an official emblem and uniforms were introduced. ''' December - Department of Foreign Language Studies (English and German) established. * {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year}} (Meiji 37) ''' March - Reorganized under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}} as an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}, with Political Science and Commerce Departments added to the Law Department. ''' October - Total enrollment in the Law, Political Science, and Commerce Departments reached 1,800, with approximately 80 instructors. * {{ill|1905|ja|1905th year}} (Meiji 38) ''' October - Courses in the Commerce Department commenced."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 69. * {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year}} (Meiji 44) ''' April - Courses in the Political Science Department began in both the university and specialized divisions."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 508–510. * {{ill|1917|ja|1917th year}} (Taisho 6) ''' April - Duration of the Preparatory Course extended to two years. * {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}} (Taisho 9) ''' April 16 * '''Reorganized as a university''' under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, establishing the Faculty of Arts and Letters (Departments of Law, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology) and the Faculty of Commerce (Commerce Department). * {{ill|1923|ja|1923rd year}} (Taisho 12) ''' March - University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year}} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year}}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year}}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year}}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year}}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism Association|url=http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx|accessdate=March 2, 2016}} == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == * Nihon University [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/9580649 "Brief {| class="wikitable" align="right" border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" style="margin:auto" |- ! colspan="2" style="background:#efefef;" |日本法律学校 |- |創立 | style="background:white;" |[[1889年]][[10月4日]]
（設立認可） |- |所在地 | style="background:white;" |[[東京市]][[麹町区]]（開校時） |- |創立者総代 | style="background:white;" |[[宮崎道三郎]]{{Cite web|和書| author = | title = 創立者宮崎道三郎と創立関係者 | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 | page= | quote = }} |- |後身校 | style="background:white;" |[[日本大学]] |} '''日本法律学校'''（にほんほうりつがっこう）は、[[1889年]]（[[明治]]22年）10月に[[東京市]][[麹町区]][[飯田橋|飯田町]]の[[皇典講究所]]内に設立設立認可。された[[私立学校|私立]][[法律学校 (旧制)|法律学校]]。[[大日本帝国憲法]]公布にともない、[[皇典講究所]]所長である[[法務大臣|司法大臣]][[山田顕義]]が、[[日本]]の[[法律]]を研究し国運の増進をはかる目的とする学校の設立をめざし、同じ趣旨で学校設立計画を進める法律学者らを全面的に支援して設立された。この項目では後身である日本大学（[[専門学校令]]準拠）についても扱う。 == 概要 == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|[[皇典講究所]]発祥記念碑]] 現在の'''[[日本大学]]の前身'''である私立法律学校である。現在の日大では本校の設立認可がなされた1889年10月4日を大学創立の日付とし、この日は同大学の「創立記念日」として継承されている 日本法律学校の設立認可からちょうど100年後の[[1989年]]（平成元年）10月4日には、[[上皇明仁|明仁天皇]]および[[上皇后美智子|美智子皇后]]の臨席のもと日本大学の創立百周年記念式典が挙行されている。{{Cite web|和書| author = 天皇・皇后| title = 主な式典におけるおことば（平成元年） | publisher = [[宮内庁]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。日大の学部・学科のうち[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]法律学科および[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|文理学部]]は「日本法律学校」時代に、法学部政治経済学科・[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]は[[専門学校令]]準拠時代（[[旧制専門学校]]としての日本大学時代）にまでその起源を遡ることができる。 [[1889年]]（明治22年）[[4月3日]]の「日本法律学校設立趣意書」の趣意では、「外来の先進ヨーロッパ諸国の法学思想とわが国固有の思想との融合調和を目指し、日本独自の法律文化を確立するため、法学教育の機関を創設すべき必要がある」とし、主意書に記されている創立目的を要約すると、「日本の法律は新旧を問わず学ぶ、海外の法律を参考として長所を取り入れる、日本法学という学問を提唱する」とした。[[近代国家]]の成立期、従来のように欧米法教育が主流の時代において、日本法律を教育する学校として誕生した本校は独自性を発揮することとなった。 開校当初は、[[皇典講究所]]の校舎を借り受けて授業を行うなど、同所および同所内に設立された[[國學院]]と深い関係を有していた。また設立当初行っていた夜間授業は最初に認可されたものである。 == 沿革 == === 設立時の経緯 === [[ファイル:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|学祖・[[山田顕義]]]] [[ファイル:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|創立者総代・[[宮崎道三郎]]]] [[ファイル:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|初代校長・[[金子堅太郎]]]] [[ファイル:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|第2代校長、初代総長・[[松岡康毅]]]] [[1889年]]（明治22年2月11日に[[大日本帝国憲法]]が発布されると、[[法学|法学界]]の中から'''外国の法理論は参考とし、日本の法律を中心に研究することを趣旨とする学校の設立'''を求める声が起こった。当時、初代[[法務大臣|司法大臣]]の任にあった[[山田顕義]]は、日本最初となるこの憲法の施行に向け日本独自の[[法典]]研究と教育が急務であると考え、自らが所長を兼ねていた[[皇典講究所]]内に「[[国法]]科」を新設することを構想した。また同時期、山田とは別に[[東京大学|東京帝国大学]]教授・[[宮崎道三郎]]を中心とする若手の法律学者らによって日本法律を教授する学校の設立の計画が進められていた。これらを契機として、山田は宮崎や憲法起草者である[[金子堅太郎]]ら法学者11名と協議し、新たな理念と思想を持つ法律学校設立のための設立要旨を次のように取りまとめた。 「一、国法は日本固有の国体・民情・慣習・ 文化を根底として作らるべきであり，この際日本古来の慣習制度をみ直す　二、憲法はじめ法律が多数制定されつつある現在，これを国民に熟知徹底させるために日本法律を講義する　三、日本法律として成立した法律を検討し，古来の精神・慣習・制度の面から必要な改正の議をたてる　四、同時に海外の法理もまた大いに研究し，わが国法学に資し，もって日本法学を振起して国運の増進をはかる」。 上記の設立要旨をもって1889年9月、[[東京府]]に設立許可が申請され、同年10月4日に設立が認可された日本法律学校は、翌年の[[1890年]]9月、設立者の一人である金子堅太郎を初代校長に迎えて開校した。開校当初、本校は皇典講究所の校舎内に設置され、同所の校舎（教室）を夜間借り受けて講義を行なう形式をとっていたが、これは同じ年の1890年、皇典講究所内に国史・国文・国法を教授する[[國學院]]が開校したことにともない、当初の山田の構想に沿って同校において国法を専修し法典研究にあたる部局として位置づけられていたためである{{Cite web|和書| author = | title = 学部・学科等の理念・目的 - 國學院大學 | publisher = | date = | url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf | accessdate = 2016-02-23 | page= 6 | quote =}}。 一方、設立評議員となった山田顕義は、設立時に示した開学理念による思想的影響に止まらず、運営財政面を中心にさまざまな形で本校の設立事業とその後の学校の発展に大きく貢献した。彼の支援によって設立時には[[司法省 (日本)|司法省]]から「法律取調事業嘱託費」の名目で50,000円の下付がなされただけでなく、設立後にも彼は[[文部省]]に対して「特別認可学校」とするよう要請を行った。さらに彼はさまざまな近代法典編纂に関わり日本における「近代法の祖」と称されていることから、本校の後身機関である日本大学は彼に「'''学祖'''」の称号を与え、大学の歴史上特別な位置づけとしている。 === 皇典講究所からの独立 === [[1892年]]11月11日、庇護者である山田が死去すると資金難が予想されたため本学は廃校も協議されるようになり、卒業生46名を送り出した[[1893年]]7月の第1回卒業式の直前には金子校長が辞職する事態となった。しかし卒業生の運動もあって本学はこの危機を乗り切り、1893年12月には[[司法省 (日本)#指定学校|司法省指定学校]]とされ[[松岡康毅]]が第2代校長に就任し、学校経営を安定させることに成功した。そして[[1897年]]には学術研究の機関誌として『日本法政新誌』が創刊されるなど、法律学校としての体裁も次第に整備された。これらと並行して[[1895年]]～[[1896年]]の校地移転、および1896年12月の[[財団法人]]改組を通じて皇典講究所からの組織的独立も果たした。 === 「日本大学」と改称 === 当初法律学科現在の[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|日大法学部]]法律学科の前身。のみを設置していた本学は、[[1901年]]10月に[[高等師範学校|高等師範科]]現在の[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|日大文理学部]]の前身。を設置して単なる法律学校に止まらない[[総合大学]]への昇格を目指すようになり、[[1903年]]8月、'''[[日本大学]]と改称'''し、翌[[1904年]]に[[専門学校令]]準拠の高等教育機関となり、併せて大学部に政治科・商科それぞれ現在の法学部政治経済学科、および[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]の前身。を併設した。 なお、校名を日本法律学校から日本大学に改めることに[[文部省]]は難色を示し、理事の[[戸水寛人]]を呼びつけて「日本法律学校なら日本の法律を教える学校なので問題ないが、日本大学だと[[大日本帝国|日本]]を代表する[[旧官立大学|国立大学]]と間違えられる恐れがある」として再考を求めた。しかし戸水は承服せず、「日本大学が駄目なら[[日本学園中学校・高等学校|日本中学]]はどうなるのか」と主張し、ついに日本大学への改称を認めさせたというエピソードが知られている[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ 日本大学への改称に尽力 戸水 寛人｜日本大学の歴史][[河岡潮風]] 『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 東都游学学校評判記]』 [[博文館]]、1909年、143-144頁『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、497-498頁。 === 大学昇格への道 === この時点では制度上[[旧制専門学校]]であった日本大学が[[大学令]]による制度上の大学（[[旧制大学]]）に昇格したのは、[[1920年]]（大正9年）4月16日である。そして、専門学校令準拠の日本大学は在籍者の卒業を待って1922年度いっぱいで廃止された『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、77頁。 == 年表 == [[File:日本法律学校（1896年頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|日本法律学校（1896年頃）]] [[File:1912年（明治45年）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|1912年改築の校舎]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|三崎町校舎（1920年竣工）]] * [[1889年]]（明治22年） ** 9月 - [[東京府]]に日本法律学校の設立許可が申請される。 ** 10月4日 -''' 設立認可'''。 * [[1890年]]（明治23年）9月 - 金子堅太郎を初代校長として開校式挙行。 * [[1893年]]（明治26年） ** 7月16日 - 第1回卒業生46名。 ** 12月 - 司法省指定学校となり判事検事登用試験の受験資格が与えられる。 *[[1895年]]（明治28年）- 校舎を大日本教育会（[[神田区]][[一ツ橋]]通）内に移転。 *[[1897年]]（明治30年）1月 - 学術研究誌『'''日本法政新誌'''』第1号が刊行。 *[[1898年]]（明治31年）12月22日 - [[財団法人]]組織に改組し、皇典講究所から組織的独立当時、[[財団法人]]化にしたのは本校が最初である。。 * [[1901年]]（明治34年）10月 - 高等師範科設置。 * [[1903年]]（明治36年） ** 2月 - 高等予備科・高等法学科を設置。 ** 8月19日 - [[校則]]を改め'''大学組織「日本大学」に改称'''。記念して徽章と制服・制帽を制定。 ** 12月 - 外国語専修部（英語・ドイツ語専修科）を設置。 * [[1904年]]（明治37年） ** 3月 - [[専門学校令]]準拠の[[旧制専門学校]]となり、従前の大学部法律学科と並んで政治科・商科を併設。 ** 10月 - 大学部法律学科・政治科・商科に在籍する学生総数は1,800名、教員総数約80名であった。 * [[1905年]]（明治38年）10月 - 大学部商科の授業開始『日本大学商学部百年史』 69頁。 * [[1911年]]（明治44年）4月 - 大学部・専門部の政治科の授業開始『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、508-510頁。 * [[1917年]]（大正{{0}}6年）4月 - 予科の[[修業年限]]を2年に延長。 * [[1920年]]（大正{{0}}9年）4月16日 - '''[[大学令]]準拠の[[旧制大学|（旧制）大学]]として発足'''。法文学部（法律科・政治科・宗教科・社会科）と商学部（商科）を設置。 * [[1923年]]（大正12年）3月 - 専門学校令準拠の大学部・大学予科を廃止。 == 創立に関わった人物 == 日本大学の「学祖」とされる山田顕義が創立に深く関わっている。 === 設立評議員 === * [[山田顕義]] * [[箕作麟祥]] * [[加藤弘之]] * [[穂積八束]] * [[児島惟謙]] * [[松岡康毅]] * [[清浦奎吾]] * [[中村元嘉]] === 創立者 === * [[宮崎道三郎]]（創立者総代） * [[金子堅太郎]]（初代校長） * [[樋山資之]]（幹事） * [[斯波淳六郎]]（幹事） * [[野田藤吉郎]]（幹事） * [[本多康直]] * [[末岡精一]] * [[添田寿一]] * [[穂積八束]] * [[平島及平]] * [[上條慎蔵]] == 歴代校長・学長・総長 == * 初代：[[金子堅太郎]]（[[1890年]]10月～[[1893年]]7月） * 第2代：[[松岡康毅]]（1893年12月～[[1923年]]9月）[[1903年]]8月に専門学校令準拠の日本大学学長、[[1920年]]4月に大学令準拠の日本大学学長、[[1922年]]3月に総長となった。 == 校地の変遷と継承 == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|日本大学開校の地（[[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）]] 設立時の校地は、先述の通り皇典講究所のあった[[東京市]]'''[[麹町区]]飯田町'''（現在の[[東京都]][[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）に所在し、木造2階建ての校舎を昼は國學院が、夜は日本法律学校が使用していた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、336-337頁。 山田没後の[[1895年]]（明治28年）10月に[[神田区]][[一ツ橋|一ツ橋通町]]（現・[[千代田区]][[一ツ橋]]2丁目）の[[大日本教育会]]内の一室を借りて移転したが、間もなく大日本教育会に合併話が持ち上がり、教室の継続使用ができなくなったため、翌年6月[[神田区]][[神田三崎町|三崎町]]3丁目の練兵場跡地の校舎に移転して皇典講究所から独立した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、401-406頁。当初の敷地は約220坪、建坪は約160坪。3つの教室と講師室、事務室などが設けられていたに過ぎなかったが、明治30年代には増築を重ねて6部屋の教室を擁する2階建て校舎となり『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、409頁、[[1912年]]（明治45年）にも改築の手が加えられた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695頁。 [[1918年]]（大正7年）には創立30周年記念事業の一環として新校舎の建設構想が浮上した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695-702頁。[[大学令]]による認可条件として施設整備は必須だったため、[[1919年]]（大正8年）12月に起工、認可間もない[[1920年]]（大正9年）5月に新校舎落成式、大正8年度卒業式、校友大会を兼ねた昇格祝賀会を行った『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、87-96頁。 三崎町校舎は現在の日本大学神田三崎町キャンパス（[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]および両学部管轄の大学院研究科が所在）に継承されている。旧飯田町校舎の所在地は現在、'''「日本大学開校の地」の碑'''が建立されている{{Cite web|和書| author = 千代田区観光協会 | title = 日本大学開校の地 | publisher = 千代田区観光協会 | date = | url = http://www.kanko-chiyoda.jp/tabid/297/Default.aspx | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 日本大学 （設立認可） |- |所在地 | style="background:white;" |[[東京市]][[麹町区]]（開校時） |- |創立者総代 | style="background:white;" |[[宮崎道三郎]]{{Cite web|和書| author = | title = 創立者宮崎道三郎と創立関係者 | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 | page= | quote = }} |- |後身校 | style="background:white;" |[[日本大学]] |} '''日本法律学校'''（にほんほうりつがっこう）は、[[1889年]]（[[明治]]22年）10月に[[東京市]][[麹町区]][[飯田橋|飯田町]]の[[皇典講究所]]内に設立設立認可。された[[私立学校|私立]][[法律学校 (旧制)|法律学校]]。[[大日本帝国憲法]]公布にともない、[[皇典講究所]]所長である[[法務大臣|司法大臣]][[山田顕義]]が、[[日本]]の[[法律]]を研究し国運の増進をはかる目的とする学校の設立をめざし、同じ趣旨で学校設立計画を進める法律学者らを全面的に支援して設立された。この項目では後身である日本大学（[[専門学校令]]準拠）についても扱う。 == 概要 == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|[[皇典講究所]]発祥記念碑]] 現在の'''[[日本大学]]の前身'''である私立法律学校である。現在の日大では本校の設立認可がなされた1889年10月4日を大学創立の日付とし、この日は同大学の「創立記念日」として継承されている 日本法律学校の設立認可からちょうど100年後の[[1989年]]（平成元年）10月4日には、[[上皇明仁|明仁天皇]]および[[上皇后美智子|美智子皇后]]の臨席のもと日本大学の創立百周年記念式典が挙行されている。{{Cite web|和書| author = 天皇・皇后| title = 主な式典におけるおことば（平成元年） | publisher = [[宮内庁]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 | quote =}}。日大の学部・学科のうち[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]法律学科および[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|文理学部]]は「日本法律学校」時代に、法学部政治経済学科・[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]は[[専門学校令]]準拠時代（[[旧制専門学校]]としての日本大学時代）にまでその起源を遡ることができる。 [[1889年]]（明治22年）[[4月3日]]の「日本法律学校設立趣意書」の趣意では、「外来の先進ヨーロッパ諸国の法学思想とわが国固有の思想との融合調和を目指し、日本独自の法律文化を確立するため、法学教育の機関を創設すべき必要がある」とし、主意書に記されている創立目的を要約すると、「日本の法律は新旧を問わず学ぶ、海外の法律を参考として長所を取り入れる、日本法学という学問を提唱する」とした。[[近代国家]]の成立期、従来のように欧米法教育が主流の時代において、日本法律を教育する学校として誕生した本校は独自性を発揮することとなった。 開校当初は、[[皇典講究所]]の校舎を借り受けて授業を行うなど、同所および同所内に設立された[[國學院]]と深い関係を有していた。また設立当初行っていた夜間授業は最初に認可されたものである。 == 沿革 == === 設立時の経緯 === [[ファイル:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|学祖・[[山田顕義]]]] [[ファイル:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|創立者総代・[[宮崎道三郎]]]] [[ファイル:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|初代校長・[[金子堅太郎]]]] [[ファイル:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|第2代校長、初代総長・[[松岡康毅]]]] [[1889年]]（明治22年2月11日に[[大日本帝国憲法]]が発布されると、[[法学|法学界]]の中から'''外国の法理論は参考とし、日本の法律を中心に研究することを趣旨とする学校の設立'''を求める声が起こった。当時、初代[[法務大臣|司法大臣]]の任にあった[[山田顕義]]は、日本最初となるこの憲法の施行に向け日本独自の[[法典]]研究と教育が急務であると考え、自らが所長を兼ねていた[[皇典講究所]]内に「[[国法]]科」を新設することを構想した。また同時期、山田とは別に[[東京大学|東京帝国大学]]教授・[[宮崎道三郎]]を中心とする若手の法律学者らによって日本法律を教授する学校の設立の計画が進められていた。これらを契機として、山田は宮崎や憲法起草者である[[金子堅太郎]]ら法学者11名と協議し、新たな理念と思想を持つ法律学校設立のための設立要旨を次のように取りまとめた。 「一、国法は日本固有の国体・民情・慣習・ 文化を根底として作らるべきであり，この際日本古来の慣習制度をみ直す　二、憲法はじめ法律が多数制定されつつある現在，これを国民に熟知徹底させるために日本法律を講義する　三、日本法律として成立した法律を検討し，古来の精神・慣習・制度の面から必要な改正の議をたてる　四、同時に海外の法理もまた大いに研究し，わが国法学に資し，もって日本法学を振起して国運の増進をはかる」。 上記の設立要旨をもって1889年9月、[[東京府]]に設立許可が申請され、同年10月4日に設立が認可された日本法律学校は、翌年の[[1890年]]9月、設立者の一人である金子堅太郎を初代校長に迎えて開校した。開校当初、本校は皇典講究所の校舎内に設置され、同所の校舎（教室）を夜間借り受けて講義を行なう形式をとっていたが、これは同じ年の1890年、皇典講究所内に国史・国文・国法を教授する[[國學院]]が開校したことにともない、当初の山田の構想に沿って同校において国法を専修し法典研究にあたる部局として位置づけられていたためである{{Cite web|和書| author = | title = 学部・学科等の理念・目的 - 國學院大學 | publisher = | date = | url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf | accessdate = 2016-02-23 | page= 6 | quote =}}。 一方、設立評議員となった山田顕義は、設立時に示した開学理念による思想的影響に止まらず、運営財政面を中心にさまざまな形で本校の設立事業とその後の学校の発展に大きく貢献した。彼の支援によって設立時には[[司法省 (日本)|司法省]]から「法律取調事業嘱託費」の名目で50,000円の下付がなされただけでなく、設立後にも彼は[[文部省]]に対して「特別認可学校」とするよう要請を行った。さらに彼はさまざまな近代法典編纂に関わり日本における「近代法の祖」と称されていることから、本校の後身機関である日本大学は彼に「'''学祖'''」の称号を与え、大学の歴史上特別な位置づけとしている。 === 皇典講究所からの独立 === [[1892年]]11月11日、庇護者である山田が死去すると資金難が予想されたため本学は廃校も協議されるようになり、卒業生46名を送り出した[[1893年]]7月の第1回卒業式の直前には金子校長が辞職する事態となった。しかし卒業生の運動もあって本学はこの危機を乗り切り、1893年12月には[[司法省 (日本)#指定学校|司法省指定学校]]とされ[[松岡康毅]]が第2代校長に就任し、学校経営を安定させることに成功した。そして[[1897年]]には学術研究の機関誌として『日本法政新誌』が創刊されるなど、法律学校としての体裁も次第に整備された。これらと並行して[[1895年]]～[[1896年]]の校地移転、および1896年12月の[[財団法人]]改組を通じて皇典講究所からの組織的独立も果たした。 === 「日本大学」と改称 === 当初法律学科現在の[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|日大法学部]]法律学科の前身。のみを設置していた本学は、[[1901年]]10月に[[高等師範学校|高等師範科]]現在の[[日本大学文理学部・大学院文学研究科及び総合基礎科学研究科|日大文理学部]]の前身。を設置して単なる法律学校に止まらない[[総合大学]]への昇格を目指すようになり、[[1903年]]8月、'''[[日本大学]]と改称'''し、翌[[1904年]]に[[専門学校令]]準拠の高等教育機関となり、併せて大学部に政治科・商科それぞれ現在の法学部政治経済学科、および[[日本大学商学部・大学院商学研究科|商学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]の前身。を併設した。 なお、校名を日本法律学校から日本大学に改めることに[[文部省]]は難色を示し、理事の[[戸水寛人]]を呼びつけて「日本法律学校なら日本の法律を教える学校なので問題ないが、日本大学だと[[大日本帝国|日本]]を代表する[[旧官立大学|国立大学]]と間違えられる恐れがある」として再考を求めた。しかし戸水は承服せず、「日本大学が駄目なら[[日本学園中学校・高等学校|日本中学]]はどうなるのか」と主張し、ついに日本大学への改称を認めさせたというエピソードが知られている[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ 日本大学への改称に尽力 戸水 寛人｜日本大学の歴史][[河岡潮風]] 『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 東都游学学校評判記]』 [[博文館]]、1909年、143-144頁『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、497-498頁。 === 大学昇格への道 === この時点では制度上[[旧制専門学校]]であった日本大学が[[大学令]]による制度上の大学（[[旧制大学]]）に昇格したのは、[[1920年]]（大正9年）4月16日である。そして、専門学校令準拠の日本大学は在籍者の卒業を待って1922年度いっぱいで廃止された『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、77頁。 == 年表 == opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|日本大学開校の地（[[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）]] 設立時の校地は、先述の通り皇典講究所のあった[[東京市]]'''[[麹町区]]飯田町'''（現在の[[東京都]][[千代田区]][[飯田橋]]）に所在し、木造2階建ての校舎を昼は國學院が、夜は日本法律学校が使用していた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、336-337頁。 山田没後の[[1895年]]（明治28年）10月に[[神田区]][[一ツ橋|一ツ橋通町]]（現・[[千代田区]][[一ツ橋]]2丁目）の[[大日本教育会]]内の一室を借りて移転したが、間もなく大日本教育会に合併話が持ち上がり、教室の継続使用ができなくなったため、翌年6月[[神田区]][[神田三崎町|三崎町]]3丁目の練兵場跡地の校舎に移転して皇典講究所から独立した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、401-406頁。当初の敷地は約220坪、建坪は約160坪。3つの教室と講師室、事務室などが設けられていたに過ぎなかったが、明治30年代には増築を重ねて6部屋の教室を擁する2階建て校舎となり『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、409頁、[[1912年]]（明治45年）にも改築の手が加えられた『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695頁。 [[1918年]]（大正7年）には創立30周年記念事業の一環として新校舎の建設構想が浮上した『日本大学百年史』 第一巻、695-702頁。[[大学令]]による認可条件として施設整備は必須だったため、[[1919年]]（大正8年）12月に起工、認可間もない[[1920年]]（大正9年）5月に新校舎落成式、大正8年度卒業式、校友大会を兼ねた昇格祝賀会を行った『日本大学百年史』 第二巻、87-96頁。 三崎町校舎は現在の日本大学神田三崎町キャンパス（[[日本大学法学部・大学院法学研究科及び新聞学研究科|法学部]]・[[日本大学経済学部・大学院経済学研究科|経済学部]]および両学部管轄の大学院研究科が所在）に継承されている。旧飯田町校舎の所在地は現在、'''「日本大学開校の地」の碑'''が建立されている{{Cite web|和書| author = 千代田区観光協会 | title = (Establishment approved) |- |Location | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} (at opening) |- |Chief Founder | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}{{Cite web|Japanese book| author = | title = Founder Miyazaki Michisaburō and Related Founders | publisher = | date = | url = http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/miyazaki/ | accessdate = 2019-04-11 }} |- |Successor School | style="background:white;" |{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} |} '''Nihon Law School''' (日本法律学校) was a private {{ill|law school|ja|法律学校}} established in October {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22) within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|lt=Institute of Japanese Classics Research}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kōjimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}}, {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}}.Establishment approved. In response to the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}}, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, the Minister of Justice and head of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, aimed to establish a school with the purpose of studying Japanese {{ill|law|ja|法律}} to promote national prosperity. He fully supported legal scholars who were advancing plans to establish a school with the same purpose, leading to its establishment. This article also covers its successor, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}} (in compliance with the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}). == Overview == [[File:皇典講究所 發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|200px|Memorial monument of the founding place of {{ill|Kōten Kōkyūjo|ja|皇典講究所}}]] This was a private law school that is the predecessor of the current '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}'''. At present, Nihon University regards the date of establishment approval of Nihon Law School on October 4, 1889, as the date of the university's founding, and this day is inherited as the university's "Founding Anniversary". Exactly 100 years after the establishment approval of Nihon Law School, on October 4, 1989 (Heisei 1), Nihon University's 100th Anniversary Ceremony was held in the presence of Emperor {{ill|Akihito|ja|明仁天皇}} and Empress {{ill|Michiko|ja|上皇后美智子}}. {{Cite web|Japanese book| author = Emperor and Empress| title = Speeches at Major Ceremonies (Heisei 1) | publisher = [[Imperial Household Agency]] | date = 1989-10-04 | url = https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/okotoba/01/okotoba/okotoba-h01e.html#D1004 | accessdate = 2016-03-02 }} Among Nihon University's faculties and departments, the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}'s Department of Law and the College of Humanities and Sciences can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon Law School, while the Faculty of Law's Department of Political Science and Economics, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics can trace their origins back to the time of Nihon University under the Specialized School Order (as an old system specialized school). In the "Statement of Purpose for the Establishment of Nihon Law School" dated April 3, 1889 (Meiji 22), it states, "Aiming for the fusion and harmony of the legal thoughts of the advanced European countries and Japan's own thoughts, and to establish a uniquely Japanese legal culture, it is necessary to create an institution for legal education." Summarizing the founding purposes described in the main statement, it says, "To study Japanese laws, old and new; to reference foreign laws and adopt their merits; and to advocate the academic discipline of Japanese jurisprudence." In the period of forming a modern nation-state, when European and American legal education was mainstream, this school, which was born as a school that teaches Japanese law, demonstrated its uniqueness. At the beginning of the school, lectures were conducted by borrowing classrooms of the Kōten Kōkyūjo, and thus had a deep relationship with the Kōten Kōkyūjo and the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} established within the same institute. Also, the evening classes conducted at the time of establishment were the first to be approved. ... == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nihon Law School}} * [http://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/ History of Nihon University] * [https://www.hamadayori.com/hass-col/school/nihondaigaku.htm Founding Location Collection / Opening Location of Nihon University] == History == === Circumstances of Establishment === [[File:Yamada akiyoshi 1.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Founder: {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} [[File:Michisaburo Miyazaki.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Chief Founder: {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}} [[File:Kaneko Kentaroh.jpg|120px|right|thumb|First Principal: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} [[File:MATSUOKA Yasutake.jpg|120px|right|thumb|Second Principal and First President: {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} In {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22), with the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法}} on February 11, there arose a call within the {{ill|legal world|ja|法学界}} to establish a school focusing on Japanese law while using foreign legal theories as references. At the time, {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, who was serving as the first {{ill|Minister of Justice|ja|司法大臣}}, considered it urgent to develop Japanese legal codes and education for the implementation of the nation’s first constitution. He envisioned establishing a "National Law Department" within the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}, where he also served as director. Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year}}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year}}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year}}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year}},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year}}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year}}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year}} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year}} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府}}. ''' December - Designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校}}, granting eligibility for judicial and prosecutorial examinations. * {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}} (Meiji 28) ''' Campus relocated to the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}, Ichibashi Street. * {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year}} (Meiji 30) ''' January - The first issue of the academic journal, "'''{{ill|Nihon Hosei Shinshi|ja|日本法政新誌}}'''," published. * {{ill|1898|ja|1898th year}} (Meiji 31) ''' December 22 - Reorganized as a {{ill|Public Interest Incorporated Foundation|ja|財団法人}} and achieved organizational independence from {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}}.This school was the first to adopt the foundation system at the time. * {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year}} (Meiji 34) ''' October - Higher Normal Department established. * {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year}} (Meiji 36) ''' February - Preparatory and Advanced Law Departments established. ''' October - Total enrollment in the Law, Political Science, and Commerce Departments reached 1,800, with approximately 80 instructors. * {{ill|1905|ja|1905th year}} (Meiji 38) ''' October - Courses in the Commerce Department commenced."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 69. * {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year}} (Meiji 44) ''' April - Courses in the Political Science Department began in both the university and specialized divisions."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 508–510. * {{ill|1917|ja|1917th year}} (Taisho 6) ''' April - Duration of the Preparatory Course extended to two years. * {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}} (Taisho 9) ''' April 16 * '''Reorganized as a university''' under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, establishing the Faculty of Arts and Letters (Departments of Law, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology) and the Faculty of Commerce (Commerce Department). * {{ill|1923|ja|1923rd year}} (Taisho 12) ''' March - University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year}} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year}}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year}}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year}}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year}}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year}}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year}}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year}}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism Simultaneously, separate from Yamada’s efforts, a group of young legal scholars led by {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburō|ja|宮崎道三郎|12=draft}}, a professor at {{ill|Tokyo Imperial University|ja|東京帝国大学|12=draft}}, was planning the establishment of a school to teach Japanese law. Prompted by these movements, Yamada consulted with Miyazaki and eleven other legal scholars, including {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎|12=draft}}, one of the constitution’s drafters. Together, they formulated the foundational principles for establishing a new law school with innovative philosophy and ideas: 1. National law should be based on Japan’s unique national character, customs, and culture. This requires reevaluating Japan’s traditional institutions. 2. With the ongoing enactment of numerous laws, including the constitution, it is necessary to educate citizens thoroughly about Japanese law. 3. Established Japanese laws should be examined, and necessary amendments proposed from the perspective of traditional customs and institutions. 4. At the same time, foreign legal theories should be extensively studied to contribute to Japanese jurisprudence, thereby revitalizing Japanese legal studies and advancing the nation’s prosperity. Based on the above principles, an application for the school’s establishment was submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府|12=draft}} in September 1889, and approval was granted on October 4 of the same year. Nihon Law School opened the following year, in September 1890, with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎|12=draft}}, one of the founders, serving as its first principal. Initially, the school was housed within the Kōten Kōkyūjo, using its classrooms during the evenings for lectures. This arrangement aligned with Yamada’s original vision, as the Kōten Kōkyūjo also established the {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院|12=draft}} that same year, which specialized in teaching national history, literature, and law. Yamada Akiyoshi, one of the school’s founding trustees, contributed not only ideologically to the establishment of the school through the founding philosophy he proposed but also significantly to its financial and operational development. During the school’s establishment, he secured a subsidy of 50,000 yen from the Ministry of Justice under the pretext of "Expenses for Legal Research Projects." After its establishment, Yamada also petitioned the Ministry of Education to designate the school as a "Specially Approved Institution." Given his contributions to compiling modern legal codes in Japan, earning him the title of "Father of Modern Japanese Law," the school’s successor institution, {{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学|12=draft}}, awarded him the honorary title of "Founding Father," recognizing his unique historical importance. === Independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo === After Yamada’s death on November 11, {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year|12=draft}}, financial difficulties were anticipated, and the possibility of closing the school was discussed. Just before the first graduation ceremony in July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year|12=draft}}, where 46 graduates received their diplomas, Principal Kaneko resigned. However, thanks to the efforts of the graduates, the school overcame this crisis. In December 1893, it was designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校|12=draft}}, granting its graduates eligibility to take the judge and prosecutor selection exams. {{ill|Matsuoka Kōki|ja|松岡康毅|12=draft}} was appointed as the second principal, stabilizing the school’s management. In {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year|12=draft}}, the academic journal "Nihon Hosei Shinshi" (日本法政新誌) was launched, marking the gradual formalization of the school as a law institution. During this period, the school also relocated its campus between {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year|12=draft}} and {{ill|1896|ja|1896th year|12=draft}}, and in December 1896, it transitioned into a {{ill|public interest incorporated foundation|ja|財団法人|12=draft}}, achieving organizational independence from the Kōten Kōkyūjo. === Renaming to Nihon University === Initially offering only a law program,The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Law at Nihon University|ja|日本大学法学部|12=draft}}. the school added a {{ill|Higher Normal Department|ja|高等師範科|12=draft}} in October {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year|12=draft}},The predecessor of the {{ill|Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at Nihon University|ja|日本大学文理学部|12=draft}}. setting its sights on becoming a {{ill|comprehensive university|ja|総合大学|12=draft}} rather than merely a law school. In August {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year|12=draft}}, the school was renamed '''{{ill|Nihon University|ja|日本大学|12=draft}}''', and by {{ill|1904|ja|1904th year|12=draft}}, it had become a higher education institution under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令|12=draft}}, adding Political Science and Commerce departments alongside its law program.These departments are the predecessors of the Political Science and Economics Department in the Faculty of Law, the College of Commerce, and the College of Economics at Nihon University. The Ministry of Education initially opposed the renaming from Nihon Law School to Nihon University, arguing that the name might be confused with national universities representing Japan. However, board member {{ill|Tomizu Hirohito|ja|戸水寛人|12=draft}} successfully countered, citing the existence of {{ill|Nihon Gakuen|ja|日本学園中学校・高等学校|12=draft}} as a precedent, ultimately securing approval for the new name.[https://www.nihon-u.ac.jp/history/forerunner/tomizu/ Contribution of Tomizu Hirohito to Renaming Nihon University | History of Nihon University]{{ill|Kawaoka Shiofū|ja|河岡潮風|12=draft}}, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/813235/95 Reviews of Schools in the Eastern Capital]," 博文館, 1909, pp. 143–144.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 1, pp. 497–498. === Path to University Status === At this point, Nihon University was still an {{ill|old-system specialized school|ja|旧制専門学校|12=draft}}. It officially transitioned to a university under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令|12=draft}} on April 16, {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year|12=draft}}. The specialized school-level Nihon University ceased operation after graduating its last students by the end of the {{ill|1922|ja|1922nd year|12=draft}} academic year.Nihon University Centennial History, Volume 2, p. 77. == Chronology == [[File:日本法律学校（1896th year 頃）.png|thumb|200px|right|Nihon Law School (circa 1896)]] [[File:1912nd year （明治45th year ）改築の校舎.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Renovated Building (1912)]] [[File:Nihon University,1920.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mishuku Campus (completed in 1920)]] * {{ill|1889|ja|1889th year|12=draft}} (Meiji 22) ''' September - Application for the establishment of Nihon Law School submitted to the {{ill|Tokyo Prefecture|ja|東京府|12=draft}}. ''' October 4 * '''Official recognition''' granted. * {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year|12=draft}} (Meiji 23) ''' September - Opening ceremony held with {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎|12=draft}} as the first principal. * {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year|12=draft}} (Meiji 26) ''' July 16 - First graduating class of 46 students. ''' December - Designated as a {{ill|Ministry of Justice-approved school|ja|司法省指定学校|12=draft}}, granting eligibility for judicial and prosecutorial examinations. * {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year|12=draft}} (Meiji 28) ''' Campus relocated to the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会|12=draft}} building in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区|12=draft}}, Ichibashi Street. * {{ill|1897|ja|1897th year|12=draft}} (Meiji 30) ''' January - The first issue of the academic journal, "'''{{ill|Nihon Hosei Shinshi|ja|日本法政新誌|12=draft}}'''," published. * {{ill|1898|ja|1898th year|12=draft}} (Meiji 31) ''' December 22 - Reorganized as a {{ill|Public Interest Incorporated Foundation|ja|財団法人|12=draft}} and achieved organizational independence from {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|12=draft}}.This school was the first to adopt the foundation system at the time. * {{ill|1901|ja|1901st year|12=draft}} (Meiji 34) ''' October - Higher Normal Department established. * {{ill|1903|ja|1903rd year|12=draft}} (Meiji 36) ''' February - Preparatory and Advanced Law Departments established. University and Preparatory Divisions under the Specialized School Order abolished."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, p. 77. == Key Figures in the Founding == {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義|12=draft}}, regarded as the "Founder of Nihon University," played a pivotal role in its establishment. === Founding Council Members === * {{ill|Yamada Akiyoshi|ja|山田顕義|12=draft}} * {{ill|Mitsukuri Rinsho|ja|箕作麟祥|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kato Hiroyuki|ja|加藤弘之|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kojima Iken|ja|児島惟謙|12=draft}} * {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kiyoura Keigo|ja|清浦奎吾|12=draft}} * {{ill|Nakamura Motoyoshi|ja|中村元嘉|12=draft}} === Founders === * {{ill|Miyazaki Michisaburo|ja|宮崎道三郎|12=draft}} (Representative Founder) * {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎|12=draft}} (First Principal) * {{ill|Hiyama Motoyuki|ja|樋山資之|12=draft}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Shiba Junrokuro|ja|斯波淳六郎|12=draft}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Noda Fujitaro|ja|野田藤吉郎|12=draft}} (Secretary) * {{ill|Honda Yasunao|ja|本多康直|12=draft}} * {{ill|Sueoka Seiichi|ja|末岡精一|12=draft}} * {{ill|Soeda Juichi|ja|添田寿一|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hozumi Yatsuka|ja|穂積八束|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hirashima Kyūhei|ja|平島及平|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kamijo Shinzo|ja|上條慎蔵|12=draft}} == Principals, Presidents, and Chancellors == * First: {{ill|Kaneko Kentarō|ja|金子堅太郎|12=draft}} (October {{ill|1890|ja|1890th year|12=draft}} – July {{ill|1893|ja|1893rd year|12=draft}}) * Second: {{ill|Matsuoka Koki|ja|松岡康毅|12=draft}} (December 1893 – September 1923)In August 1903, Matsuoka became the President of Nihon University under the {{ill|Specialized School Order|ja|専門学校令|12=draft}}, and in April 1920, he was appointed President under the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令|12=draft}}. In March 1922, he became the Chancellor. == Campus Relocation and Legacy == [[File:Nihon University Place of opening.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Site of Nihon University's original campus in {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chiyoda|ja|千代田区|12=draft}}.]] The original campus was located in the {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|ja|皇典講究所|12=draft}} in {{ill|Iidamachi|ja|飯田町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kojimachi Ward|ja|麹町区|12=draft}} of {{ill|Tokyo City|ja|東京市|12=draft}} (modern-day {{ill|Iidabashi|ja|飯田橋|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chiyoda City|ja|千代田区|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|12=draft}}). It was a wooden, two-story building shared with {{ill|Kokugakuin|ja|國學院|12=draft}}, used by the law school in the evenings."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 336–337. After the death of Yamada in November {{ill|1892|ja|1892nd year|12=draft}}, financial difficulties prompted the school to consider closure. However, in October {{ill|1895|ja|1895th year|12=draft}}, the campus relocated to a rented space within the {{ill|Greater Japan Education Association|ja|大日本教育会|12=draft}} building on Ichibashi Street in {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田区|12=draft}}. The merger of the association soon made continued use of the facility untenable, leading to the 1896 relocation to the former drill grounds in {{ill|Misakicho|ja|神田三崎町|12=draft}}, Kanda Ward, marking the institution’s formal independence from Kōten Kōkyūjo."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 401–406. The initial Misakicho campus measured approximately 220 tsubo (727 m²) with a building footprint of around 160 tsubo (529 m²), housing three classrooms, a lecture room, and offices. By the 1910s, it had been expanded into a two-story structure with six classrooms."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 409. The facility underwent further renovation in {{ill|1912|ja|1912nd year|12=draft}}."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, p. 695. In {{ill|1918|ja|1918th year|12=draft}}, plans for a new campus emerged as part of the university’s 30th-anniversary celebrations."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 1, pp. 695–702. Meeting the facility requirements of the {{ill|University Ordinance|ja|大学令|12=draft}}, construction began in December {{ill|1919|ja|1919th year|12=draft}}. The new campus was completed in May {{ill|1920|ja|1920th year|12=draft}}, coinciding with the university’s graduation ceremony and promotion celebration."Nihon University Centennial History," Volume 2, pp. 87–96. The Misakicho campus now forms part of Nihon University’s Kanda Campus, housing the {{ill|Faculty of Law|ja|日本大学法学部|12=draft}}, {{ill|Faculty of Economics|ja|日本大学経済学部|12=draft}}, and affiliated graduate schools. The original site in Iidamachi is commemorated by a monument reading "Site of Nihon University's Founding."{{Cite web|title=Site of Nihon University's Founding|publisher=Chiyoda City Tourism
